abstract: For reflector antennas, if the feed horns have the conventional characteristic, just like the single mode horns from Kelleher, the requirement of simultaneous high gain and low side lobes is impossible, In this paper, the designed and measured results of a shaped beam doubly curved reflector antenna are given. The E-plane 10 dB level beam width of it's feed horn is about 1.7 times that of the 3 dB level beam width (the H-plane is 1.82 ). Compared with the feed horns that has 1.82 E- and H- plane beam width ratios like Kelleher's, the gain of the antenna is not changed, but the side lobes were reduced about 4 dB.

Author Keywords: Shaped beam doubly curved reflector antenna

articleTitle: A New Dual Band Branch-Line Coupler Using Coupled Lines
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new Dual band branch line coupler (BLC) using coupled transmission lines that can operate at two arbitrary frequencies, is introduced. The analysis of the structure is based on the even-odd mode analysis of conventional BLC as well as a new equivalent circuit which composed of a coupled transmission line and two transmission lines. This new dual band BLC has miniaturized size and planar structure. For verification purposes, simulated results of a micro-strip branch line coupler that is designed for 900/2000 MHz are included.

articleTitle: Ray Tracing Method for Ground Penetrating Radar Waves
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Ray tracing is the key to ray-based GPR simulations and tomography. We develop a ray tracing method for GPR transmission and reflection based on the wave front expanding approach. It is a flexible and available means to determine the transmitted and reflected ray paths. Its main advantage over the conventional methods is that it can trace the curved ray within a strongly heterogeneous media, and find simultaneously all reflected ray paths from one complicated interface for a pair of transmitter and receiver. Several numerical testing examples show its good results.

articleTitle: On the Accuracy of Finite Difference Analysis for a Shielded Microstrip Line in a Quasi-Static Aprroach
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Quasi-static analysis of the shielded microstrip line is performed with Finite Difference Method (FDM), and related potential and electromagnetic field distributions are obtained. Transmission characteristics are computed through the potential distribution and compared with the ones calculated by the approximate explicit expressions. The accuracy of finite difference analysis is discussed.

articleTitle: Improved Reflection and Transmission Coefficients of Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: An improved reflection and transmission coefficients are developed for treating electromagnetic problems of scattering from frequency selective surfaces (FSS). The incident field is decomposed into parallel and perpendicular component to the plane of incidence<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>, correspond to reflection and transmission coefficients are given, which are simple formally and applicable to all incidence.

articleTitle: Analysis of Special Interference Methodologies in Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper the effects of interference of non-geostationary orbit (GSO) satellite with GSO satellite services is calculated. As these effects are calculated in frequencies up to 30 GHz, the interference with the assumption of given GSO satellite parameters (such as BER C/N) is determined considering rain fade. For calculation of C/I in this paper, we first introduce various methodologies which are used to calculate maximum allowable level of interference. Then using these methodologies, EPFD (the equivalent power flow density) is calculated. Finally, a computer program is developed using one of these methodologies and comparison is made with an ITU (International Telecommunication Union) model which shows good agreement.

articleTitle: New Method of Velocity Compensation in a Stepped-Frequency Testing Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A solution on velocity compensation for a dual-channel stepped-frequency testing radar is presented. The target's radial velocity was estimated real-timely by using high resolution range profiles of the target from two bands respectively, and then compensation was carried out to get the target's real location for automatic target range tracking. An effective method to calculate target's real location avoiding complex computation in direct compensation procedure is discussed. Experimental results are also given and analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of Settling Time of One Dimension Nonlinear Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Beam scanning and beam forming can be achieved by nonlinear antenna array technology without the need of phase shifters. The architecture and settling time of phase distributions of nonlinear antenna array is studied in this paper. A general equation describing the phase dynamic of external locking array, unilateral locking array and mutual locking array is deduced. Transient response of nonlinear antenna array is analyzed. The analytic formula of settling time is presented.

articleTitle: EMC Design of Multi-PLL System with High Isolation Performance
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: First introduced the theory of PLL, analyzed the factors in the multi-PLL system that may affect the isolation. Then employing EMC theory analyzed and designed the multi-PLL system. At the end, presented the results of isolation measurements. The methods used in the design are especially useful and helpful for the design of multi-channel receiver.

articleTitle: New Method for Synthesis of a Narrow Beam in Linear Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A enetic algorithm is used for optimization of beam forming in linear array antennas. The goal is to achieve a narrow beam-width of about 1 degree with a linear array of parabolic antennas. Simulation shows about 80 % beam-width reduction.

articleTitle: Scattering Characteristic Simulation and Analysis of Two Stealth Aircrafts
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Radar scattering characteristics of two stealth aircrafts are simulated and analyzed in this paper. The software FEKO is used for the simulation. The simulation result well agrees with the experimental data. MOM and PO hybrid algorithm is used to maintain the precision and accelerate the computing speed. According to the simulation data and figures, stealth characteristic is analyzed. Considering the complexity of the models and the computing ability of personal computer, some detailed parts of the model plane are not constructed.

articleTitle: Coupled Cavity Waveguides Consisting of Two-Dimensional Electromagnetic Crystals Formed by Rectangular Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A full wave method for modal analysis of coupled cavity waveguides consisting of layered arrays of rectangular cylinders is described. The mode propagation constants and the mode field profiles can be derived by an improved Fourier series method, which is of very simple form, and is always suitable for all the arrays of arbitrary profiles, any depth, and any permittivity. The dispersion equation is expressed by using generalized reflection matrices.

articleTitle: Implementation and Performance Analysis of a Tri-Pole Filter for Scanning Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A tri-pole filter is proposed as a video integrator for scanning radar. Coefficients optimization of the tri-pole filter is carried out via genetic algorithm (GA) which evaluates the fitness of individual using a new function in time-domain. The tri-pole filter requires only 0.1 dB increase in signal-to-noise ratio to provide the same detection capability as the optimum integrator. Moreover, it has better stability than two-pole filter because the distance between its poles and unit circle is further. The tri-pole filter is analyzed and it is shown that its performance is superior to that of the two-pole filter.

articleTitle: Element Antenna Design for a Two-dimensional Aperture Synthetic Millimeter-wave radiometer
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: An aperture synthetic radiometer makes use a large number of, sparsely distributed, radiometers to achieve high resolution (special and radiometric) measurements. Each element radiometer has its own element antennas, the specifications of which strongly influence the final performance of the aperture synthetic radiometer. Therefore, in designing element antennas, one must consider the restrictions posed by the aperture synthetic radiometer requirements such as antenna size, beam-width and mutual coupling, etc. In this paper, we present an example of element antenna design, which is suited for a 8 mm band two-dimensional aperture synthetic radiometer.

articleTitle: A Processing Detection Project Research of Weak Targets in the Complex Ground Clutter
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The paper present a project of improving the weak targets detection capability in the complex ground clutter at the same time maintaining the hardware's simplicity for the air-ground millimeter-wave terminal guidance radar. The project use the wide band chirp-subpulse stepped-frequency signal to detect targets, and get the target region's quasi two dimension image by processing the echo signal both in the time and frequency domain, thereby improving the weak target detection capability and providing the real guidance information. The theoretical analysis and computer simulation result proved the project's validity.

articleTitle: Piecewise Integration for Conformal FDTD Method to Reduce Staircasing Errors
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Attention is focused on a new conformal FDTD method. The contour-path value of the electric field component can be obtained more accurately by the piecewise integration. Several examples are simulated to demonstrate the proposed method. Numerical results show that the PI-CFDTD method provides increased accuracy and stability over the conventional CFDTD method.

articleTitle: Breakdown and Transmission of High Power Microwave Beam
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Considering the pondermotive force, the transmission of high power microwave beam after air breakdown is studied. It is put forward that for long pulse beam, high-repetition pulses beam and continuous wave beam, the process of air breakdown and transmission is different compared with uniform plane wave. The uneven electric-field distribution will lead to redistribution of electron concentration and will finally form a low density channel, which will allow the microwave energy to transmit fluently. Finally, the breakdown and transmission characteristics of very short pulse, repeated pulses and continuous microwave are analyzed individually.

articleTitle: Numerical Dispersion Analysis of FETD Method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The finite-element time-domain method (FETD) has been developed in order to simulate the complex electromagnetic structures. In this paper, an analysis of the numerical stability and dispersion of this method are presented. It is found that the stability is strongly depended upon the the temporal step size, and the numerical dispersion is bounded by the ratio of the carrier wavelength to the spatial step size. And, in comparsion with the the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, the FETD is proven to be advantaeous in the problems of large scale objects.

articleTitle: A Simple Approach of Resource Allocation in Antenna-Array Based OFDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Applying smart antennas to an OFDMA system is investigated. A simple resource allocation scheme for array-antenna based OFDMA systems is proposed. The resource allocation algorithm is applied to the pilot data when no beam is formed and channel estimation in frequency-domain is implemented. After piloting, a beam is formed for each user to enhance the performance of the system. Simulations based on the SUI channel model according to the standard of IEEE 802.16e WMAN are carried out to examine the performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Radar Target Signature Measurement Using DBF Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Radar target signature is usually measured using step frequency radar system, in which the beam of antenna can not be changed. According to the need of the measurements, various beam width, various frequency band width and various beam scanning angle can be chosen. Digital beam forming technology can be applied to promote the measurements to a new level. Not only the desired main lobe can be got, but also the side lobe can be lowered. In addition, digital beam forming appears better efficiency in calibration and scanning adaptively.

articleTitle: The Non-Intrusive Feeder Lines of Antennas Failure Testing Approaches
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we introduce several fundamental non-intrusive feeder lines of antennas failure testing approaches, analyze and evaluate results of several failure testing experiments using the testing approach based on infrared imaging, discussing developing of non-intrusive feeder lines of antenna failure testing technology based on infrared imaging.

articleTitle: Techniques of Band-Broadening for an Inverted-F Antenna used in WLAN
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper is to present a design method for a PIFA antenna, which can be used to cover the resonant frequency range both of IEEE 802.11a standard and IEEE 802.1 lb/g standard individually. Especially, The band of 802.11a is almost covered fully as a wideband, instead of only individual narrow bands. This PIFA antenna is based on the traditional concept of transmission line antenna. Physically, it is a double-sided PIFA antenna with different width at some parts of its horizontal section. Both of simulated and measured results are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis and experiment of transition between micro-strip and a miniaturization substrate integrated waveguide (SIW)
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The paper firstly study dispersion characteristics of the miniaturization SIW, and then study the problem of transition between this structure and micro-strip. This paper mostly researched the directly transit form, then designed a Ku-band planar transition between micro-strip and the miniaturization SIW. The results of simulation show that the insertion loss excelled than 0.5dB in the designed frequency band, so it has the applied worthiness.

articleTitle: Analysis of Longitudinal Slot in the Broad Face of Rectangular Waveguide Using the MPSTD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the MPSTD algorithm is applied to model longitudinal slot in the broad face of rectangular waveguide. Firstly, an approach of dividing the total-field and the scattered-field is proposed based on the characteristic variables of Maxwell's equations. And the updating equations of the field on the interface between the scattered-field domain and the total-field domain have been derived. Secondly, the setting of excitation source is proposed by the idea of domain partition, which makes the domains of incident-field, scattered-field and total-field contacted availably. So it is convenient to introduce the incident-field and calculate the scattered-field. The resonant length and impedance characteristics of longitudinal slot are analyzed by MPSTD. The numerical results indicate that the MPSTD algorithm is accurate and efficient to analyze the longitudinal slot in the broad face of rectangular waveguide.

articleTitle: A Novel Unsupervised Iteration Classification Method For Fully Polarimetric SAR Image
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Based on the theory of eigen-decomposition of fully polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and scatter criterion clustering method, an unsupervised iteration classification method is proposed. It is simple, flexible and with high precision. Several schemes of the iteration classification method are given in this paper. The characteristic of each scheme is carefully analyzed according to the properties of eigen-decomposition and scatter criterion, and each scheme holds its own merit. Experiments are done on SIR-C/X-SAR data near Tien Mountains and perfect classification results are obtained. More importantly, this method is robust and has high adaptability.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Disc-Loaded-Coaxial Waveguide for Wideband and High-Gain Gyro-TWTs
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Field-matching technique was used to analyse a disc-loaded-coaxial waveguide in the azimuthally symmetric TE modes for its dispersion relation that includes space-harmonics in the disc-free region as well as modal-harmonics in the disc-occupied region of the structure. The phase propagation constant, obtainable from the dispersion relation, was fed back in the small-signal gain-equation of the gyro-TWT and the gain-frequency response of a disc-loaded-coaxial gyro-TWT was plotted. Further, the effect of the radius of coaxial rod insert on gain-frequency response has been studied, and the parameter has been optimised for high gain and wideband of the device.

articleTitle: Beams-based Space--time Decoding in Multi-path Fading Environments
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, performance of beams-based transmit diversity in a multi-path fading channel is investigated. At the transmitter, Alamouti' s coding signals is transmitted by two independent transmitting beams. Since the received signals at each receive antenna encompasses all the multi-path components from every transmitting beam, a technique is proposed to combine the space-time block coding signals and implement space-time decoding. Simulations are conducted to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: 2-D FDFD Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering by Complex Targets
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The formulations in finite-difference frequency-domain (FDFD) computational domain are obtained from Maxwell's equations. The absorbing boundary and total-field boundary are analyzed in detail in order to simulate electromagnetic scattering problems in open region. The incident wave is introduced by setting equivalent electromagnetic currents on the total-field boundary. In order to save memory and speed up the solving speed, a compressed storage scheme and the conjugate gradient method are adopted respectively. The Kirchhoff surface integral representation is used to calculate the far field from the FDFD near field data . Numerical examples are presented to verify this method.

articleTitle: Method-of-Moments solution for the Probe-Excited cavity Problem
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In order to solve the impedance matching problem encountered in the rectangular waveguide filter design, the corresponding modeling, parameter extracting and designing are presented. The moment method is introduced to analysis the input impedance of the probe located in an arbitrary position of the waveguide broad side, then, with the use of 3 cavities solution, a 2-port scattering matrix is derived. The computed result coincides well with Ji-Fuh Liang's measured results. At last, an example for a dual-mode waveguide filter verifies the validity of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Absorption Properties of Materials under Microwave Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The paper presents dielectric relaxation processes of materials that is a key physical phenomenon in the fields of microwave chemistry, microwave detection and microwave processing of materials. Using the new equation for the description of dielectric losses under microwave irradiation, which was developed by authors, absorption properties of rubber compounds was simulated. It was found that the simulating results based on this new equation are in good agreement with the Volge-Fulcher law. It shows that the new equation has potential application in the study of microwave interaction with materials.

articleTitle: Calculation of EM Scattering Property of Rough Surface by the BMIA\CAG
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In the low grazing angle (LGA) incidence problem of rough surface, the surface length must be long enough which corresponds to a large matrix's dimension. If the method of moment is used directly, the computational speed will be very slow. In this paper, the banded matrix iterative approach\ canonical grid method (BMIA\CAG) combined with MOM is applied to calculate the large scale scattering problem of rough surface. The speed is greatly accelerated by this arithmetic, the larger the dimension, the more the times than MOM. Then, the influence of bandwidth of the matrix to the arithmetic is analyzed. At last, the bistatic scattering coefficient of fractal rough surface is gained at LGA case.

articleTitle: A Plane Wave Scattering by a LHM Anisotropic Uniaxial-coated Conducting Sphere
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: On the basis of spherical vector wave functions in uniaxial anisotropic left-handed materials (LHMs) and the first, second, third and fourth spherical vector wave functions in uniaxial anisotropic LHMs satisfy the same differential equation, the electromagnetic fields in uniaxial anisotropic LHMs can be expressed as an addition of the first and second spherical vector wave functions in uniaxial anisotropic LHMs. Applying the boundary conditions of electromagnetic fields in the interface between LHMs and free space, in the surface of conducting sphere, the expansion coefficients of electromagnetic field in uniaxial anisotropic LHMs and scattering field in free space can be derived, and then the radar section cross (RCS) of a plane wave scattering by a LHMs anisotropic uniaxial-coated conducting sphere. Some numerical results are given in this paper.

articleTitle: A Concise Derivation of Flat Earth Effect and Terrain Height Effect for Across-track InSAR
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Based on the spatial geometry relationships, a concise derivation of the flat earth effect and the terrain height effect is illustrated for across-track InSAR systems. The interferometric phase can be expressed in the form of a sum of these two kinds of effects through the derivation. The influences of the flat earth and the terrain height to the interferometric phase are simulated, which are in accordance with the theoretical analysis. The flat earth effect and the terrain height effect for distributed SAR systems are also discussed.

articleTitle: The Anti-jamming Performance of GPS/SINS Integrated System in White Noise Jamming Environments
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper discusses the anti-jamming performance of the track loop of receivers in GPS/SINS integrated system, analyses the differences between anti-jamming performance of GPS/SINS integrated system with white noise jamming and that of C/A code receivers. Then the theoretical conclusion is validated through the jamming experiment of immited signals to C/A code receivers. It is testified that C/A code GPS/SINS integrated system has a better anti-jamming performance that may reach 40 dB above.

articleTitle: FDTD Modeling for tree-trunk scattering on the soil
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents our global approach to model Ultra Wideband (UWB) FOPEN (Foliage Penetration). In this approach, we consider plane wave scattering (in time domain) from the tree trunks above the soil. The time-domain scattering is computed via FDTD method, which is particularly well adapted to frequency-dependent soil. This method is processed prior to a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), which is performed to come back to the frequency domain. Thus, we may have rich information for applicability to the FOPEN detection need.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Terahertz Horn Antenna Based on MEMS Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper studies one kind of new type antenna, which works at about 0.3 ~ 1.5THz. The antenna is designed by using finite element method (FEM), and its structure is based on realizable micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) technology. The antenna structure design depends on the physical characteristics of the material silicon and the existing technics of MEMS technology. This form of antenna cell is easy to integrate. The simulation result of a 4×4 antenna array is also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Light scattering by a multilayered infinite cylinder immersed in an absorbing medium
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Analytic solutions are developed for a single-scattering properties of an inhomogeneous cylinder embedded in an absorbing medium with normal incidence, and the rapid recursive algorithm is given. Some examples are simulated to validated the code, and the scattering phase-matrix is discussed at last. The Study is important for both active and passive remote sensing.

articleTitle: Presenting a Method for Wide Band Nulling by Spiral Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Spiral phased array antenna nulling is presented. The array factor and classic method for spiral array antenna proposed here. Proposed method and genetic algorithm for optimization of fixed nulling in spiral array antenna are used and compared. The goal is to achieve a -20 dB in null over the wide frequency band. Our simulation shows -20 dB over 75 MHz null bandwidth, in VHF band by GA and over 90 MHz null bandwidth by proposed design method.

articleTitle: The PCB Power/Ground Resonant Impedance Damping Based on The Cavity Resonant Model
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The power bus structure in PCB or IC, which is consisting of two parallel planes separated by an insulator, behaves as a cavity resonator. The high resonant impedance at certain resonant frequency between the IC or PCB's power and ground layers is the cause of some signal integrity problems. Based on the theory of parallel planes cavity resonator, this paper deducts the relation functions between the resonant impedance, resonant frequency, resonant quality factor and the electromagnetic parameters of power/ground planes structure. By using the deductions above, this paper investigated 2 main new ways to reduce the resonant impedance, which are using magnetic substance or graphite as plane conductor material and adopting insulator material with high permittivity and loss tangent. And the effects of the two ways above in resonant impedance damping are expressed clearly by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on Typical Millimeter Wave Radar Target Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The advantage of millimeter wave radar, radar cross section (RCS) and one dimension range profile are presented at this paper. With the high frequency approximate method, the typical millimeter wave (35 GHz, 94 GHz) radar target characteristics are simulated. With the comparison, it is found that the target's radar cross section at 94 GHz has more details and evident scattering centers, but the range profiles have similar scattering centers with the same band.

articleTitle: Preconditioned Multilevel Fast Inhomogeneous Plane Wave Algorithm for Solving Electromagnetic Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A mesh-neighbor preconditioner is implemented into the multilevel fast inhomogeneous plane wave algorithm (MLFIPWA), to solve three dimensional electromagnetic scattering problems more efficiently. The spectrum integration of the Green's function and grouping technique are used in FIPWA to translate the direct source and field interaction into aggregation, translation and disaggregation, to accelerate the matrix-vector multiplication. The computation complexity of this algorithm is O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4/3</sup>). By applying a multilevel strategy, this complexity can be reduced to O(N log N) . To further speed up the solution process, a mesh-neighbor preconditioner is applied into this fast algorithm. Numerical results show the accuracy and efficiency of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi-mode Microwave Remote Sensing Antenna Subsystem on Satellites
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents briefly design, assembly and testing of the multi-mode microwave remote sensing antenna subsystem of China. It concentrates active and passive microwave remote sensors. A prime focus paraboloid reflector, with the diameter of 600mm, is applied as the altimeter antenna. The scatterometer antennas consist of two prime-focus reflectors, which take conical scanning and form two pencil beams orthogonal in space and polarization. The radiometer antenna is an offset paraboloid reflector with multi-frequency, dual polarization and common aperture feed. Computer aided integrated design for multi discipline, advanced assembly and holographic measuring techniques, which are used to achieve high accuracy, are also introduced.

articleTitle: Using New Material to Analyze Doppler-shift Arising From Change of the Solar-angle
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: From simple theory of Chapman, we deduce a formula to calculate Doppler-shift arising from change of the solar-angle. We compare the result of theory with new material-Doppler records of BPM and JJY ,and analyze the reasons of producing difference.

articleTitle: Effects of Structure Parameters and Stress for Capacitive Switches MEMS Bridge on Time Response
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel method for analyzing the switching time of the electrostatic driven RF MEMS capacitive switches is presented. The effects of the structure parameters which mainly include the width, length and thickness and stress for capacitive switches MEMS bridge on time response are investigated using the SYNPLE module of IntelliSuitetrade tool. The result shows that the width of MEMS bridge and the stress in bridge indistinctively affect on time response, while the length and thickness of MEME bridge distinctively effect on time response.

articleTitle: Design of One Kind of Multilayer Microstrip Antenna Working at Dual-frequency and Treble-polarized
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Two electromagnetic signals which have orthogonal both phase and space can generated one circular polarized (CP) signal, in the opposite hand, one CP signal can separates into two lineal polarized signals. One kind of strip fed multilayer microstrip antenna using cross-slot coupling is discussed in this paper. Constructed of one right-hand-circular polarized (RHCP) and one left-hand-circular polarized (LHCP) antenna cell, an antenna array is designed out in this paper. By choosing appropriate feeding circuit, the antenna array is designed to work at dual-frequency on 12.75 Ghz and 14 Ghz, fed separately by three dividedly ports, it can radiate vertical, horizontal, 45deg to horizon lineal polarized signals separately. The according PCB to this design worked well at this very dual-frequency.

articleTitle: Study on the Micro-Oscillation Phenomenon of Bent Microstrip Line
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The micro oscillation phenomenon of bent microstrip line is investigated in this paper by FDTD method and FFT. The micro oscillation phenomenon actually is due the small discontinuity in the bent region. In this paper, a Gaussian pulse is excited into the bent microstrip line, and the oscillation phenomenon is then studied by analyzing the waveform of reflected pulse of the bend and the corresponding frequency spectrum. The relationship between the oscillation and the structure parameters of the bent microstrip line is given.

articleTitle: A Dual Frequency Small Loop Antenna Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The genetic algorithm is employed to optimize the dual frequency matching network for a small size loop antenna. The antenna is optimized to work at 4~5MHz with VSWR less than 2.5 and 30 MHz VSWR less than 1.5, respectively. A real antenna is built and its test results are in good accordance with the calculated ones.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Analysis of H Waveguide Filled with Laminated Dielectric Slab
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: H guide is a semi-open guide wave structure applied in millimeter waves. In this paper, H guide filled with laminated dielectric slab is analyzed by using the method of lines-full wave analytic method, and characteristic equations of this guide in different modes are obtained. Calculated characteristic equations of double-strip H guide are in good agreement with relative references, and the analytic method can be demonstrated credible. The analytic model in this paper is also suitable for analyzing NRD guide.

articleTitle: Passive Temperature Sensing Tag for Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A novel passive temperature sensing tag for a long reading range composed of a divided microstrip antenna and a rectifying circuit boosting the DC voltage is proposed. Experimental study of fabricated passive tag using varactor diodes, in which 30 m range response can be achieved in the 4 W EIRP reader at 860-960 MHz band, is described. Passive tags for temperature-monitoring system in the 4 W EIRP reader at 2.45 GHz band are also fabricated to demonstrate validity of proposed tags for a range longer than 9 m. The tags have sizes of 90 times 60 times 4 mm and 60 times 25 times 4 mm for 900 MHz and 2.45 GHz bands, respectively.

articleTitle: Unequally Valued Emitter Ballasting Resistors Optimum Design of Multi-finger Power GeSi HBTs
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Multi-finger structure is commonly used in microwave power GeSi HBTs (heterojunction bipolar transistors). Usually equally valued emitter ballasting resistors are added to improve thermal stability of the devices. However, self-heating and thermal coupling effects make the temperature distribution on emitter fingers non-uniform, so the equally valued ballasting resistors structure is not optimum. In this paper, an unequally valued ballasting resistors structure is presented, which could improve the uniformity of devices' temperature distribution effectively, and decrease the highest temperature to a certain extent.

articleTitle: An Efficient Canonical-Grid Method for Scattering from Rough Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: An efficient canonical-grid (ECG) method for wave scattering from perfectly conducting random rough surfaces is proposed. In this new method, the Taylor series expansion of the Green's function about a flat horizontal surface is replaced by interpolating polynomials using zeros of Chebychev polynomials as interpolation points. The convergence rate of the Chebychev interpolating polynomials is more rapid than that of Taylor series expansion, which extends the applicability of the standard canonical-grid (SCG) method to rougher surfaces.

articleTitle: Studies on Radial Three-Cavity Coaxial Virtual Cathode Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new radial three-cavity structure of the coaxial virtual cathode oscillator is proposed and studied numerically in this paper. Using the radial three-cavity structure, the beam-wave conversion efficiency is enhanced by modulating the E-field in the beam-wave interaction area, whereas the resonator composed of the radial three-cavity configuration and the mesh anode helps restrain mode competition efficiently. Also, the output microwave power is improved by the coaxial extraction structure in respect that it benefits the energy extraction and it can also absorb the used electrons entering into the drifting tube. With an electron beam of 400 kV and 50 kA, a peak instantaneous power about 6 GW is achieved by simulation at 4.14 GHz. The peak period-averaged power reaches 2.45 GW and the beam-wave conversion efficiency is about 12%. The output microwave has high mode purity and narrow bandwidth.

articleTitle: Study on indoor wireless overlay of mobile communication system
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: With the development of mobile communication, quality of indoor communication is highly demanded by mobile consumers. This paper analyses the characteristic of indoor wireless communication system, studies ray-tracing method and bring forward the key points for designing indoor wireless communication.

articleTitle: Derivation of the Second Electric Dyadic Green's Function Based on the Method of Gm
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The eigenfunction expansions of the second electric dyadic Green's function for a half infinite coaxial waveguide can be derived based on the method of Gm, whereby the irrotational vector wave function L is not needed. This work presents detailed derivation, in which scattering superposition and boundary condition on dyadic tangential magnetic field are used. The result can be directly used to analyze EMI caused by slot and aperture coupling.

articleTitle: Design of spherically stratified microwave lens used for antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Study is made on the scattering problem of a plane wave incident on a spherically stratified microwave lens. Then, the radiation field of the lens exited by an open-ended waveguide is calculated by the use of coordinate transformations and reciprocity theorem. Good agreement between the theoretical prediction and the measured radiation characteristics is observed. Finally, curves useful for the design of the spherically stratified microwave lens are presented.

articleTitle: Broad-Band Matching Networks for Active Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: To the problem of low efficiency and big size for broad-band and electrically small antenna, we refer to the positive resistor method of broad-band matching network for active antenna. Using the method, we analyze and research for the radiant characteristic of active antenna. To realize miniaturization, broad-band, higher radiant efficiency and higher correspondence quantity for antenna in wireless communications, the study result has important applied value.

articleTitle: A Simulation Study on the Blackbody Emissivity Measurement Using Bistatic Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Blackbody emissivity measurement is necessary in order to calibrate the microwave radiometers. One of the methods for determining blackbody eimissivities is to employ bistatic radar. To understand the measurement accuracy, a simulation study is done using techniques of numerical electromagnetics, equivalence theorem and reaction integral equation, which describes the relation-ship between the incident wave, the blackbody scattering and the received power of the receiving antenna.

articleTitle: Volume Integral Equation using Solenoidal Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper studies the application of the basis functions proposed by Carvalho and Mendes (1999), which are defined on tetrahedrons, in the analysis of the electromagnetic scattering problem of the three-dimensional homogeneous or inhomogeneous dielectric objects. Necessary formulations for implementation, especially the process of singular integral emerged in the method of moments are given by a mathematical trick. Numerical results suggest that the proposed approach is a effective one.

articleTitle: The Influence of Electron Beam Thickness on the Characteristics of a Coaxial-waveguide CARM Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The influence of electron beam thickness on saturated power and efficiency of a coaxial-waveguide cyclotron autoresonance maser (CARM) amplifier is presented.

articleTitle: Optimal Simultaneous Extrapolation of Electromagnetic Responses in Time and Frequency Domains Using Laguerre Expansions
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, an optimal simultaneous extrapolation algorithm of electromagnetic responses in time and frequency domains using Laguerre expansions is adopted to calculate the electromagnetic responses of medium cylinders excited by linearly polarized wave with a Gaussian profile in time. By using an optimization algorithm, the expansion order and scaling factor can be found that leads to accurate extrapolation. The numerical results are testified to be very efficient.

articleTitle: Target Detection with Non-Cooperative Illuminators
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The main features of target detection based on non-cooperative illuminators is introduced in this paper, develop status quo of passive radar and basic structure of the system presented, and the key techniques which are required for implementing the system and their current development described.

articleTitle: A New Nonlinear Companding Method for Reducing Peak-to-Average Power Ratio of OFDM Signals
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: How to reduce the Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) signals has become one of the key problems in OFDM system. By analyzing the reason of high PAPR, a new nonlinear companding method is proposed to reduce the PAPR in this paper. Then we give the optimal value of the parameter in this scheme. At last, our simulation results confirm that the suggested scheme exhibits good performances in both time and frequency domains by comparing with other methods.

articleTitle: A Simple Method to Optimize the Ballasting Resistor of RF Power HBT
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Taking into account of the temperature dependence of emitter junction voltage, the valence-band discontinuity at emitter junction (DeltaE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sub>), and the bandgap narrowing due to heavy doping (DeltaE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>), a simple method to optimize the ballasting resistor of RF power heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) has been presented based on the thermal-electric feedback network analysis. The agreement between theory and experiment is shown to be excellent. Using this design flow, we can choosing the best ballasting resistor of power HBT needed for thermal stable operation under the specified working condition.

articleTitle: Scattering Centers Measurements by a 2-D ESPRIT Type Method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A 2-D ESPRIT type method is presented for the scattering centers measurements in step-frequency radar. This method estimates the signal parameter pairs directly unlike the matrix enhancement and matrix pencil (MEMP) method which contains an additional step to pair the parameters related to each dimension. We use a forward-backward prediction data matrix to increase the estimation accuracy and the robustness to noise. Results compared with the Fourier transform method show that the resolution and precision of the 2-D ESPRIT type method are both higher than those of the Fourier method.

articleTitle: Improvement on the Forward-backward Iterative Physical Optics Algorithm Applied to Computing the RCS of Large Open-ended Cavities
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The method of initial value succession is introduced to the forward-backward iterative physical optics (FBIPO) algorithm. The initial residual error is reduced by inheriting the current values. Combined with a relaxation parameter, the method improves the convergence of the FBIPO algorithm for cavity scattering problems. The accuracy of RCS calculation is also enhanced by using a more precise mixed-face model. Then, the RCS of a jet inlet model is calculated, with its results in good agreement with the experimental ones. The method is also used to calculate the RCS reduction of a circular waveguide by coating the inner wall with a thin absorber layer.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Radar Signature Simulation of Complex Targets
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper describes an approach to the simulation of radar signatures from large complex targets. Due to the difficult problems of actual measuring and scaling measuring for the signature of large-scale radar targets under the condition to wideband, an effective approach of computing high-frequency radar cross section (RCS) to complex targets is presented in advance, and then the target's ID range profile can be obtained. The result suggests that it is possible to obtain satisfying simulated radar signature using this approach.

articleTitle: The model and key technique researches of atmosphere laser communication system
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we analyzed the key techniques of wireless optical communication system, and established the typical weather model by outside survey in different weather conditions, designed parameters of the source coding and the channel coding. Simulated it by Matlab. The emulational results indicated that the communication capability was enhanced by using 256-PPM (the source coding) and RSldr 255,223ldr (the channel coding).

articleTitle: A Novel Noncoherent Monopulse Processing Scheme and Its Channels Imbalance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The noncoherent processing can alleviate the effect of phase imbalances in receiver channels of monopulse radar. In this paper, a novel noncoherent processing scheme, which uses logarithmic amplifiers, is considered and explicit expressions are derived for the indicated angle as a function of various imbalances in the receiver channels. Its performance is then analyzed using shift in null position and deviation in slope of the angle sensitivity curve as criteria. Its performance in some aspect is superior to that of the conventional monopulse processing due to symmetrical channels and wide dynamic range.

articleTitle: Design of X-band Microstrip Ring Reflectarray Antenna with Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A microstrip reflectarray antenna is a flat reflector antenna which consists a thin reflecting surface made up of many individual elements and an illuminating feed. This kind of antenna has many good characteristics than traditional parabolic reflectors, such as low profile, easily deployable, lower manufacturing cost and scannable beam. A 200 mm-diameter microstrip reflectarray antenna is designed by using MOM-based commercial EM software FEKO. The maximum right hand circularly polarization gain is 19 dB and the sidelobe level is -18 dB at 8 GHz. The aperture efficiency is 40% and the circular polarization axial ratio is 2 dB.

articleTitle: MOM Analysis of Cylindrical Conformal Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper intends to search for the analytical solutions for the singular integral in analyzing conformal dipole arrays by method of moments (MOM). For the integral kernel of dipoles, an analytical solution is obtained by using the series form of the complete elliptic integral of the first kind. A recursive relation and an analytical solution are obtained to eliminate the singularities of the self-impedance integrals of the body of revolution (BOR). And the nonsingular parts of the integrals of the BOR are numerically integrated by FFT. Finally, a cylindrical conformal dipole array is analyzed by the method proposed above. The results agree well with those of measured.

articleTitle: A High-Frequency Pulse Transmission System on Human Body Area: Simulation and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: With the rapid progress of electronic and information technology, an expectation for the realization of body area network (BAN) has risen. In this study, we proposed a pulse transmission system with frequencies at dozens of megahertzes. The system was based on an impulse radio (IR) scheme with bi-phase modulation. By using the frequency-dependent finite difference time domain (FD2TD) method, we investigated the on-body transmission characteristics and derived a path loss expression. We also investigated the influences of Gaussian noises and other narrow-band interferences on the communication link budget and bit error rate (BER) performance.

articleTitle: Multi-binding Scheme for Simultaneous Mobility of MIPv6
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Simultaneous mobility is the case when both hosts are mobile nodes and they move at about the same time. The simultaneous mobility problem is that messages, especially protocol messages, are lost during simultaneous mobility, which leads to the interruption of communication, and handoff delay. This paper analyzes simultaneous mobility problem for MIPv6 and some current solutions, and proposes multi-binding solution based on home agent. Experiments showed this scheme can resolve such problem effectively and efficiently.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Diversity Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: To increase link gains and enhance performance in wireless systems, antenna diversity has long been used. Such diversity provides a means not only to overcome the effects of signal multipath andfading in realistic RF channels or propagation environments but also to increase channel capacity. In this paper, we propose a design that uses hybrid combining of two types of antenna diversity, spatial and polarization, for a consistently better received RF signal. The design is adaptive in that it periodically tests signal strength on a number of channels, and selects those which provide the better signals at that time. A four-choose-two system was developed andprototyped. About 5 dB in power gain over the reference non-hybrid system was achieved. A significant reduction in signal power variance (about 2.3 dB) was also observed experimentally.

articleTitle: Broadband CPW-fed Circular Wide-Slot Antenna with Circular Tuning Stub
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A printed circular wide-slot antenna fed by the coplanar waveguide (CPW) with circular tuning stub for wide-band applications is proposed. Results show that the impedance matching of this kind of antenna is greatly affected by the size of the tuning stub and the slot, and the spacing between the stub and the ground plane. By properly choosing the suitable the radius of the slot and the stub, selecting the distance of the centers and tuning their dimensions, designs with significantly enhanced impedance bandwidths are obtained.

articleTitle: The Laser Remote Sensing of Underwater Acoustic Signal
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Some underwater targets can give off regular sound wave. When the pressure change due to underwater acoustic signal fluctuation transmitting to the water surface, it may cause slight disturbance at the interface between water and the air, which means that the reflected laser beam carries the information of the underwater acoustic signal since the corresponding laser beam has been modulated. Some necessary information can be obtained through photoelectric detection, demodulation and wave transformation of the reflected or scattered beam of laser. Integrated the transmission characteristics of acoustic signal under seawater with the one of laser beam in free space, one new laser remote sensing technology is suggested which is an effective way to recognize underwater targets and realize on-board active scanning, acquisition, pointing and tracking over a wide range. Experiments validate the feasibility of laser detection of underwater acoustic signal.

articleTitle: The Automatic Testing Software for Electromagnetic Emission Based on Labview
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper introduces the condition, requirement and method of automatic testing for electromagnetic emission of electronic equipments and discusses in detail how to design the automatic testing software with Labview program to realize the structure and constitute of the software based on GPIB. The method and ideas of this paper can also be applied to the software design of other electronic equipments.

articleTitle: A Study on Visualized Field Distribution of Intensive Microwave Field
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The measurement of the distribution of intensive microwave field based on a new method which is put up by designing a testing container and 'Multi-channeled, Synchronous, Temperature sampling and processing system' in this paper. Applying the method, it is possible to describe the distribution of microwave field and achieve the visualization of the distribution of microwave power by use of MATLAB. It is proved by experiments that this method is feasible and reliable.

articleTitle: Conical beam control of arbitrary conical spiral antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The conical beam forming characteristics of a two-arm and a four-arm conical spiral antenna with arbitrary configuration are researched in this paper. The antennas are analyzed based on the Nakano integral equation and the moment method. The results show that their beam direction can be changed by adjusting the winding denseness of the antennas. With the increase of the winding denseness their beam deviation from the axis increases to form conical shaped radiation patterns. The beam deviation of equiangular conical antennas from the axis is wider than that of Archimedean conical antennas. Archimedean conical antennas are better than equiangular conical antennas in beam conformity.

articleTitle: Design of Substrate Integrated Waveguide Sum-Difference Comparator
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The model and software simulation of a novel substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) sum-difference comparator based on 3dB-coupler with 90deg phase delay is proposed. Equivalent model parameters are initially used to determine geometric sizes and then numerical simulation is applied to make optimization and obtain electrical characteristic variations and electro-magnetic field distributions. An example comparator is presented for operating at 9 GHz, together with S-parameters curves and field distributions. This comparator can be used in minimized direction-finding radar systems.

articleTitle: The Optimal Incident Polarizing Angle in the Portable Optical Sensor for Electromagnetic Measurement
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The research of the measuring methods for electromagnetic pulse has important significance. The principle and the scheme of the optical sensor based on magneto-optic crystal are introduced. The effect of the linear birefringence and incident polarizing angle on the output performance of the sensor are derived using Jones Matrix. The research of the optimal incident polarizing angle is made. The results show that when the incident polarizing angle is set to some special values the sensitivity of the system to the linear birefringence will be minimized and the system performance can be optimized.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Sidelobe Planar Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the effect of array aperture distribution errors is considered and discussed, and a low sidelobe planar array antennas is synthesized. Through theory analyzing and calculating, the low sidelobe design method is obtained, and the design criterion is given. Furthermore, the results that considered the effect of array aperture distribution errors are compared with the ideal results that obtained from the Taylor line source method. It is shown that the sidelobe levels (SLLs) are enhanced because of the effect of feed aperture distribution errors. Thus the design method has a better application.

articleTitle: On Fast Computation of Electromagnetic Wave Propagation through FFT
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The Taylor Interpolation through FFT (TI-FFT) algorithm for the computation of the electromagnetic wave propagation in the quasi-planar geometry within the half-space is proposed in this article. The optimized computational complexity of the planar TI-FFT algorithm is N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</sup>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</sup>O(Nlog<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>N) for an N = N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>×N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub> computational grid, where N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</sup> is the optimized number of slicing reference planes and NOopt is the optimized order of Taylor series. Detailed analysis shows that N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</sup> is closely related to the algorithm's computational accuracy <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">γTI</sub>, which is given as N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</sup> ~ -ln <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">γTI</sub>, and the optimized spatial slicing spacing between two adjacent spatial reference planes only depends on the characteristic wavelength λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of the electromagnetic wave, which is given as δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</sup> ~ 1/17 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>. The planar TI-FFT algorithm allows a large sampling spacing required by the sampling theorem. What's more, the algorithm is free of singularities and it works particularly well for the narrow-band beam and the quasi-planar geometry.

articleTitle: Using Level Restoring Method for Dual Supply Voltage
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new level converter for use in dual voltage SOI digital circuits is presented. The technique which uses the idea of keeper transistors, consumes less power compared to the traditional methods. The effects of load capacitance on the circuit are studied by extensive simulations.

articleTitle: Naturally Derived Turbulence Measurement Procedures
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Atmosphere turbulence is described in terms of a general formulation that does not assume any particular form foe the turbulence structure function. Expressions are obtained for the tow-point correlation function of the complex amplitude (i.e., the atmospheric MTF) and for the more general function, the tow-point two-wavelength correlation function of the complex amplitude. A cardinal set of measurement procedures naturally derives from these two functions that enable both the integrated strength and the average structure function of the turbulence in a propagation path to be characterized. The measurement procedures are based on certain key properties of point-object images; properties that carry the essential information about the integrated effects of all mechanisms in the propagation path that affect the wavefronts. These mechanisms can include, but are not limited to, atmospheric turbulence, boundary layer turbulence, thermal blooming, telescope aberrations, and the (corrective) effects of adaptive optics. The measurement procedures enable full end-to-end characterization of the entire propagation path between object and image. They take account of amplitude scintillation as phase variation in the wavefronts. Once the entire path has been characterized, a wavelength region can be identified that leads to optimum resolution from large ground-based astronomical telescopes. For HEL system, use of optimum wavelengths leads maximum irradiance at the target and maximum target lethality range. Large performance improvements are attained by use of optimum rather than non-optimum wavelengths.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Design of Microwave Filters with Direct Source-Load Coupling
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a method for synthesizing microwave filters with source-load coupling. The equivalent circuit of the low-pass prototype of a general lossless coupled resonator filter is proposed, and the corresponding transfer function t(s) is derived. Then, two microstrip filters with source-load coupling, one symmetric and the other asymmetric, are designed, and the simulations are completed. The evaluated and simulated data are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Super-resolution Direction Finding at Subarray Level for Coherent Sources Based on Weighting Network
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: 2-D subarray level super-resolution direction finding methods have important applications in phased array radars. This paper studies ML (Maximum Likelihood) method at subarray level suitable for coherent sources and gives the corresponding signal model. Applying simplified array manifolds can make calibration cost of phased array reduced largely. We post-process the digital subarray outputs by bringing in weighting network which increases the flexibility of array processing greatly. The simplified array manifold based on Gaussian patterns we constructed can overcome the limitations of DSAM (Direct Simplified Array Manifold) method that available direction estimation area can't be changed and the uninterested sidelobe sources can't be suppressed completely, but the cost is that the precision of direction finding drops. Simulation results demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Backscattering from the Time-varying Oceanic Surface with Consideration of Multiple-scattering
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A multiple-scattering method is formulated to calculate the backscattering from time-varying dielectric oceanic surface. The theoretical prediction is compared with the experimental data, and reasonably good agreement is obtained. Much attention is paid to discuss the amplitude distribution of the scattered field when the surface varies in a random way, and these theoretical results are compared with the classic distributions to find the best fitting.

articleTitle: A Reliable UWB Based Routing Scheme for Industrial Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Standard wireless technologies are envisioning for the development in industrial environments. Major obstacles toward the fulfillment of industrial application are that how to solve the reliability and real-time requirements. The routing protocols play an important role for ultra-wideband (UWB) based wireless networks performance. A new routing scheme suitable for UWB based industrial wireless network was proposed in the paper. The new routing scheme utilizes orientation of UWB and tries to get enough route information and guarantee reliable dissemination to all nodes in the network. Simulation results show that the new routing protocol achieves reliable data communication and with more energy efficiency than SPIN (sensor network protocols using information negotiation).

articleTitle: Analysis of Millimeter Wave Conformal Antenna Array on Conical Surface
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Microstrip antenna (MSA) is quite flexible and has been used as conformal antenna mounted on arbitrary surface. Conformal finite-difference time-domain (CFDTD) method has shown excellent versatility. In this paper, CFDTD is applied to analyze microstrip patch antenna mounted on conical surface. Based on the analysis, an omnidirectional 4times4 millimeter wave (MMW) conformal microstrip antenna array which works at 35 GHz is developed. The measured data shows good agreement with simulation.

articleTitle: A Modified Helix antenna with Gain Improvement and Size Reduction
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new modified helix antenna is introduced which combines the helix and monopole together and forms improved current distribution. The character makes it more convenient for gain improvement and size reduction. The antenna is designed and simulated with Ansoft HFSS which is based on Finite Element Method (FEM). According to the rule, some models are fabricated for use on two-way radio. The measured results are presented and prove the theory efficient.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Broadband Low-Profile Two-Strip Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A broadband low-profile monopole antenna is analyzed by using balanced and unbalanced mode decomposition. The broadband antenna consists of an S-strip and a folded T-strip that are separately printed on the two sides of a thin planar substrate, forming a two-strip monopole. The two-strip antenna can achieve a bandwidth (VSWRles2) of ~40% with a height of 0.08lambda<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. It is revealed that the broadband performance of the two-strip antenna is a result of the combination of an unbalanced mode and a balanced mode. Experimental results verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Application of The Microgenetic Algorithm to The Optimization of Multilayered ZnO Whisker Radar Absorbing Coating
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: An optimization method based on the microgenetic algorithm (MGA) is presented for the design of multilayered radar absorbing materials made of tetrapod-shaped ZnO whisker. The optimization procedure is designed for a given thickness and the optimization conditions, which are different in order to meet the practical requirements in the different frequency bands (the range of 2~18GHz). The effects of the thickness, the number of layers, and the restrained conditions on the optimization results are discussed in detail.

Author Keywords: multilayered radar absorbing materials tetrapod-shaped ZnO whisker

articleTitle: Study of Band-gap Characteristics for Curved EBG Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: According to the reflection condition of optics Bragg, a curved EBG structures is designed, and the band-gap characteristics of it is studied deeply. The effect of EBG structure parameters and cylindrical structure parameters on band-gap characteristics are analyzed for the first time, and some useful conclusions are obtained, which have an important guided significance to applied to curved conformal antennas.

articleTitle: Design of Efficient Nonuniform Microstrip Couplers
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the idea of using optimum designed nonuniform microstrip couplers is proposed to design efficient wideband couplers. A nonuniform microstrip coupler is considered and optimally designed using a proposed least mean square method. The usefulness of the proposed structure is verified using a comprehensive example.

articleTitle: The investigation of directional coupler based on a novel synthetic transmission line
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A novel synthetic transmission line and its coupling structure are shown in this paper. By connected strips in different layers with periodic metallic vias, it provides a stronger coupling with effective broad-side than conventional edge coupling. This paper presented the analysis method and the design process of directional coupler. A broadband directional coupler with three-sections is designed and measured.

articleTitle: A Simple Differential Calibration Scheme for Multi-channel Errors in DOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The presence of gain and phase errors between array elements and corresponding channels is known to significantly degrade the performance of most high resolution direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithms. In this paper, a simple calibration scheme is proposed to eliminate the errors existing in the multiple channels of a direction finding (DF) system equipped with a uniform circular array (UCA). Based on differential calculations and second-order statistics, the new calibration method can compensate the differences between the channels effectively with lower implementation complexity. The design process of the scheme is described and discussed in detail. Both theoretical analyses and Monte-Carlo simulations are also provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering by Charged Dust Aggregates
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Dust aggregates in plasma charge, which makes it difficult to study the propagation of electromagnetic wave in it. While in order to study the influence of charged dust to the space detection, some work must be done for the electromagnetic characteristic of it. Based on discrete dipole approximation (DDA), electromagnetic scattering characteristic of charged dust aggregates is studied. At the beginning, DDA theory and expressions of scattering coefficients by a single charged sphere are introduced simply. Nextly, considering the influence of charges, the polarization of each dipole in DDA method is corrected by scattering coefficients of charged sphere. Thirdly, the models of charged dust aggregates we using are simulated by two different methods. Thus, combing the correction polarization index with the DDSCAT package, the scattering intensities of a plane wave by charged dust aggregates can be calculated, and the influence of quantity of electricity, which we express it as surface conductivity , to the scattering fields of it can also be analyzed in detail. The study of electromagnetic scattering by charged dust aggregates will play an important role in the atmospheric optics, astrophysics, remote detection and other fields.

articleTitle: Theoretical Study of Wideband Antenna Using High Efficiency Impedance Loading Profile
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: On the basis of Wu-King current distribution, the author extends it to the double exponential current distribution, modifies the inaccurate part of the Wu-King resistive loading profile and deduces a high efficiency non-reflecting loading profile. The electrical properties of the high efficiency non-reflecting loading antenna have been studied theoretically; the concept of lengthening coefficient is created and the optimum parameter design curve of the antenna is provided. Theoretical calculation shows that the maximum bandwidth and efficiency of antenna can be achieved with this kind of loading profile simultaneously. The impedance bandwidth of antenna is as high as 40:1, which is much greater than the 3:1 bandwidth of Wu-King profile when the voltage standing wave ratio is below 3. The efficiency of antenna is about twice of the Wu-King loading antenna.

articleTitle: The Theoretical Investigation of Reflections in Anechoic Chambers
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper evaluates the characteristics of the electromagnetic field in an anechoic chamber. By using the geometrical optical approach and tracing method, the reflectivity level of the anechoic chamber is computed. The factors that may affect the reflectivity level and computing errors are analyzed.

articleTitle: A Research for the Single-Channel Time Difference Direction Finding System Model for UWB Signal
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new research about time difference direction finding system based on the single-channel model for ultra-wideband (UWB) signal is described in this paper. In contrast to multiple-channel, the single-channel direction finding system is provided with lower cost, smaller size, and better mobility. Also the character of time difference is high precision, quick direction finding .etc. [3] A new single channel modal is proposed. The research also shows that precision of the single-channel direction finding system based on time difference approaches multiple-channel one.

articleTitle: The Study of Spectral Element method in Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The application of spectral element method in electromagnetics is developed in this paper. It is extensively used in the computing mathematics. In this paper, the EM scattering problem is discussed by spectral element method. The comparision is made between finite element metheod and spectral element method.

articleTitle: Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Method for the Analysis of an Electromagnetic Wave Tool
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In the finite element method (FEM), the matrix equation can be solved either using a direct elimination method or an iterative method. The conjugate gradient (CG) is a common-used iterative method. But there are several limits in its application. In order to overcome the disadvantages, a preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) method based on the incomplete Cholesky decomposition is introduced in this paper. And this PCG method is applied to the analysis of an electromagnetic wave tool.
