articleTitle: Anti-jamming Analysis on the behavioral Modeling of Digital Communication Receiver
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a new design method for predicting anti-jam capabilities of the whole digital communication receiver based upon behavioral-level simulation techniques. Detailed design procedure is presented to describe particular design of the bit error ratio (BER) specifications of the radio frequency (RF) receiver of a direct sequencing spread-spectrum (DSSS)/binary phase shift keying (BPSK) system. This method is validated by employing the behavioral modeling in advanced design system (ADS) of Agilent company.

articleTitle: A Design of Coupled Transmission Line Filter For UWB System Using PSO Method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel method called PSO to design the coupled transmission line filter for UWB system. After detailed theoretical analysis and numerical simulation, parameters of layout for UWB coupled transmission line filter are given. Then, it was implemented on PCB. The simulation and measured results showed that, as a kind of novel optimization method, PSO is proven to be very effective for designing microstrip filters.

articleTitle: On the Time Sequence Control of Exciting Pulses for UWB Array
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The time sequence control scheme of exciting pulses for ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna array is investigated in consideration of the angle-dependent pulse distortion in UWB short pulse radiation. For a linear UWB antenna array with 5 rectangular aperture antennas as elements, three different time sequence control scheme, viz. the conventional initial-range delay scheme, the peak-range delay scheme, and the center-range delay scheme, are compared. It is shown that due to the angle-dependent pulse distortion in UWB short pulse radiation, the use of the peak-range and center-range delay scheme result in a 7% increase of the maximum radiated field intensity and a 10% increase of the maximum peak-to-peak value of the radiated electric fields if compared to the radiated field excited by the traditional initial-range delay scheme.

articleTitle: Calculation And Optimization Of Quiet-Zone In RF Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper introduces the standing wave method to test quiet-zone and geometrical-optics method to calculate quiet-zone, and compare the results of these methods. At last , two ways to optimize the value of quiet-zone are discussed. This paper has great value in design and test of microwave anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: The Omni-directional Dipole Antenna Structure and Design
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The design relates generally to the field on antennas and more specifically, to a low profile linear polarized H-shape dipole antenna. The antenna includes a printed circuit board that has a dielectric substrate provided with H-shape face and one dipole element formed on the dielectric substrate. The printed circuit board is also provided with a balance to unbalanced feed network that is operatively connected to the H-shape dipole arm element. In this design, the H-shape dipole antenna fed network with tapered balun is studied. The design and experimental results of low profile microstrip planar dipole antenna with tapered balun shows fairly good performances in this paper. The feed network of the design with wider bandwidth and lower power loss tapered microstrip line to overlap coplanar stripline (CPS) transition that provided unbalanced to balanced line with balanced equal power output of phase. The achieved planar dipole antenna exhibits 421MHz for VSWR=2 bandwidths. Full-wave EM analyses shows good agreement with those experimental data.

articleTitle: Eighth Wavelength Small Patch Antenn
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A novel eighth wavelength patch antenna is presented in this paper. The VSWR, gain and radiation pattern of this antenna are simulated. The results are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Adaptive Nulling Methods with Multiple Constraints for Transmitting DBF
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Adaptive nulling methods with multiple constraints for transmitting digital beamforming (DBF) of uniform linear arrays (ULA) are proposed in the following three circs, with main lobe constraint only, with main and side lobes constraints, with main and side lobes constraints and given nulls constraint. And the optimum weight vector of transmitting DBF is derived by Lagrange multiplier approach and calculated with sample matrix inversion algorithm. The computer simulations show that the proposed methods are practicable and effective.

articleTitle: Physical Optics Computation of Objects Modeled with NURBS Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: With the development of computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM), nonuniform rational B-spline (NURBS) is applied in describing models broadly, for example: aeronautic, automobile, ship and so on. NURBS is a very excellent method describing models, but it is harder than Bezier on computation. So the NURBS surfaces are transformed into Bezier surfaces. Thus, PO is used to compute the RCS of model with Bezier surfaces in this paper.

articleTitle: Excitation of Surface Plasmons Achieve Total Absorption of Electromagnetic Wave in Overdense Plasma
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The energy transformation from electromagnetic wave (EMW) to surface plasmons which achieve total absorption of EMW in overdense plasma is investigated by using the theory of hydrodynamics in the thin cylinder limit and surface wave resonator (SWR). The experiment scheme of Bliokh [Phys. Rev. Lett. 95, 165003 (2005)] is improved. Through analyzing the frequency domain spectrum of the reflected wave, the time series of reflection, transmission and plasma density are diagnosed when the electromagnetic wave is transferring into the surface wave (SW).

articleTitle: Circular SAR Imaging Approximated by Spotlight Processing
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the differences between circular synthetic aperture radar (CSAR) and traditional linear synthetic aperture radar are briefly analyzed with mathematical model of CSAR introduced. To verify the conclusion that CSAR can get much higher resolution than traditional linear SAR can, even with the same radar parameters, we present an approximation method using linear spotlight SAR to simulate CSAR and show the simulation results. How to fuse spectrums of all subapertures is described in detail.

articleTitle: Time-Hopping MN-ary Biorthogonal Pulse Amplitude Position Modulation for UWB Communication System
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The system performance is analyzed using a new modulation scheme called time-hopping(TH) MN-ary biorthogonal pulse amplitude position modulation(MN BPAPM) for ultra wideband(UWB) systems with asynchronous multiple- access interference (MAI) in an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel. Closed-form expressions of symbol error rate (SER) and channel capacity are provided, then the simple expressions are obtained. The performance of TH MN BPAPM and MN-ary orthogonal PPM(MN OPPM) schemes are compared in terms of the SER in the end. It is shown that the TH MN BPAPM provides better performance with lower demodulator complexity that the TH MN OPPM system. Meanwhile, for the TH MN BPAPM system, the larger N leads to lower system SER and higher channel capacity.

articleTitle: Design of a millimeter-wave tapered-slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The design and experimental results of a millimeter-wave tapered-slot antenna are presented in this paper. The antenna operates in X-band with a gain of 6 dB and a side lobe level of 10 dB. It can be easily conformed to missile and used as a fuze antenna.

articleTitle: Investigation of Complex Permittivity and Permeability of Ferrimagnet in Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In order to investigate the dielectric and magnetic parameters of soft ferrimagnet in millimeter waves, several yttrium iron garnet (YIG) and hexagonal ferrite ceramic (HFC) are measured. The complex permittivity and permeability of the YIG and HFC have been obtained in a broad-band spectrum. Measurements are realized by using a broad-band quasi-optical millimeter-wave system with a backward-wave oscillator as the source of tunable coherent radiation. Moreover, the alternating-direction-implicit finite-difference time- domain method has been used to simulate the YIG and HFC models. The experiment results are in good agreement with the numerical curves. It is shown that these results provide an accurate characterization of soft ferrites as well as hard anisotropic ferrites in the entire millimeter-wave range.

articleTitle: A New Kind of Microstrip-Fed Folded Planar Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a new kind of microstrip - fed folded planar monopole handset antennas is proposed. The effect of the structural parameters on the impedance and radiation characteristics of the antenna is analyzed by using FDTD method. The results of FDTD are essentially agreement with experimental results. The proposed antenna has properties of simple structure, broadband, and almost omnidirectional radiation within operating bands. This kind of folded planar monopole handset antenna provides a new choice for the third generation mobile communication system.

articleTitle: An electromagnetism analysis of absorber structure based on FEM/GA
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, genetic algorithm (GA) is used for getting the unknown electromagnetic parameters of multi-layer absorber structure. For this aim, a finite element method (FEM) model was brought forward and a test system based on free-space method was founded. From comparing reflection coefficients came from calculated and measured, electromagnetic parameters of unknown layer can be gotten efficiently. For improving precision, normal distributed random variable is used in genetic algorithm. Compared with transmission/reflection method, this result can be proved rightly and efficiently. This method can be used for both high and low materials.

articleTitle: Analysis of EM Scattering from 3-D Dielectric Objects by Moment Method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, EM scattering of homogeneous dielectric objects of regular geometry shape such as sphere cylinder cube is analyzed by moment method(MoM). Equivalent theory is used to analyze the characteristic of dielectric. The numerical results are compared to results using analytic method. It is found that they tally well.

articleTitle: Computation of Electromagnetic Fields inside Three Dimensional Inhomogeneous Dielectrics Using a Buffered Block Forward Backward Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The paper is concerned with the electromagnetic scattering from a three-dimensional inhomogeneous dielectric object. In particular, the paper compares the use of a buffered block forward backward (BBFB) algorithm to the use of the commonly employed weak form of the CG-FFT method for the numerical solution of the resultant electric field integral equation (EFIE). The BBFB method is based on the spatial segmentation of the dielectric into smaller pieces. Results are shown which illustrate the convergence of the algorithm and its superior performance to the CG-FFT.

articleTitle: A Simplified Two-Dimensional PWTD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a simplified two-dimensional plane-wave time-domain (PWTD) algorithm based on the existing PWTD algorithm. The scheme simplifies the translation procedure of evaluating the far fields, and then the computational cost is decreased efficiently. The derivation and examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and facility that the simplified algorithm achieved.

articleTitle: The Study of Active Periodical Structure's Reducing Surface's RCS
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Reducing radar cross section(RCS) of aerocraft's surface effectively is key issue at the field of plane steal. Structural absorb is present in this paper, using the periodical surface's character of band gap and impedance transition of electromagnetic crystal structure such as PBG, FSS and HIS, put single or multilayer periodical structure on the surface of the shell of aerocraft, and put the varactor diode onto the approximate HIS to join each cell of metal on top layer to realize the electronic control for periodical structure, will establish the active periodical structure. This structure could realize absorbing the exotic electromagnetic wave and restraining surface wave on it. The result of above process is reducing the RCS of the surface effectively. The simulation test prove that this method and technology could reduce RCS 3~14 dB at working frequency band by using single or double layer active periodical structure, and the working frequency band could be tuned by electronic method.

articleTitle: The System Design of a Small Caliber MMW Earth Observing Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: To attain a small caliber millimeter-wave earth observing radar, a wide-band miniature MMW system is needed. In this paper, the miniature system design of a frequency-modulated stepping MMW radar is presented. Firstly, this miniature radar's advantage is analyzed for the need of small caliber earth observing missile. Then, the system configuration is provided to obtain the high range resolution and miniaturization. And in the meanwhile, the method to solve new system problems and optimized selection of system parameters is discussed according to the small caliber terminal guidance radar. At last, experiment results are also given to proven the designed system 's performance.

articleTitle: Research on TA as Lidar receiver
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper compared the perfornances of Lidar system using telescope with TA (telescope array). The different perfornances including antenna gain and pattern of telescope and TA are given in this paper. The analyses results show that TA is better than telescope in Lidar system. Adaptive receive telescope array technique is described in this paper.

articleTitle: Uniaxial Perfectly Matched Layer for 2-D FETD Method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, Gedney's uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) is used for finite-element time-domain (FETD) method. And two-dimension resonance cavity is simulated by using FETD with the UPML absorbing boundary condition. The results consistent with analytical solution verify the validity of UPML in 2-D FETD.

articleTitle: A STBC Coded VBLAST Scheme for OFDM Communications Based on IEEE 802.16d
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a space-time coded VBLAST scheme for OFDM communication based on IEEE 802.16d protocol. At the transmitter, the data stream is partitioned into several groups and each group is STBC encoded and OFDM modulated independently. At the receiver, conventional VBLAST detection techniques can be employed. The SUI channel model which is recommended by the IEEE 802.16d working group is used in the simulations to compare performance of the STBC coded VBLAST scheme with that of the classic VBLAST for IEEE802.16d-based OFDM systems at the same spectrum efficiency.

articleTitle: The Design of varactor Tuned Semi-elliptic Function Microstrip Filters
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: As we need to add varactors at the edge of resonators while design varactor tuned filters, so the electromagnetic field will be changed greatly as the control voltage changed, it's extremely disadvantaged to semi-elliptic function filters as they have special demand on coupling, so we haven't see any report on voltage controlled semi-elliptic function filters. Through the additional weak couple between the input line and the output line, there will appear two transmission zeros from the normal band-pass filters, and thus achieved a novel type of semi-elliptic function filters; on the other hand, from change the couple structure of the traditional semi-elliptic function filters, we can also achieve varactor tuned semi-elliptic function filters, and thus find a new way for the design of varactor tuned semi-elliptic filters.

articleTitle: Analysis Conducting Antennas Using TD-EFIE
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: To analysis antennas in time domain using the implicit EFIE which based on the method of moment was studied. A new method, adding the inspire voltage source directly in time domain, was proposed. Simply through FFT the data of time domain, the ultra wide band frequency data can be obtained. Calculating time was greatly saved compared to the method of analysis in the frequency domain point by point. Two antennas were considered, the validity and stability of the method was proved.

articleTitle: Transient Scattering by Arbitrary Wires and Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The time-domain electric field integral equation (EFIE) is used along with marching-on in time for treating problems of transient scattering by arbitrary wires and surfaces. The conducting wire and surface are modeled by straight segments and planar triangular patches for numerical purposes. Comparisons of surface and wire current densities and backscattered far fields are made with the results from the inverse discrete Fourier transform (IDFT) of frequency-domain solution, and good agreement is obtained in each case.

articleTitle: Study of Light-scattering properties of bare substrates
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Light scattering provides a powerful tool for bare substrate and thin films characterization. Angle-resolved light scattering has been used to quantify the surface roughness of optical components. However, light scattering properties are different between opaque substrate and transparent substrate because angle-resolved light scattering is affected by the contribution of both interfaces of the transparent substrate, it cannot be applied to transparent substrates. The light scattering properties of opaque and transparent substrate were described respectively in this paper and light scattering properties of transparent substrate were analyzed in detail considering of the effects of both interfaces of transparent substrate.

articleTitle: Distortion and Delay of Laser Pulse Propagation in Sand and Dust Storm
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The pulse distortion and time delay of laser nanosecond pulse propagating through the atmosphere including sand and dust storm layer are investigated mainly at 0.69 and 3.8 mum, respectively. It is shown that the delay of 10ns laser pulse propagating through 5km sand and dust storm with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> = 1.630 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> / m3 are about Ins and 10 ns, at 0.69 and 3.8 mum, respectively. The pulse spread of a 10 ns laser pulse is over 40 ns at 3.8 mum. The pulse delay and spread increase rapidly with the sand particle density increasing in atmosphere. The narrower the pulse width is, the more the pulse distortion is. Hence, for a laser pulse propagating in sand and dust atmosphere, the pulse delay and distortion are quite severe and need be taken into account for a narrower pulse laser system.

articleTitle: Noise Analysis and Measurement of Active Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The noise of an active receiving antenna is analyzed in this paper. The design criterion and some design consideration for short wave active receiving antenna is given. The method to measure the noise figure of the active receiving antenna is proposed. It is simple, efficient and no extra request for the detection performance of the measuring instrument. The experimental confirmation shown that this method is correct.

articleTitle: Integrated Design and Research of Ka-band Electronically Large Mono-pulse Planar Antenna and Feed System
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a scheme of electrically large mono-pulse circularly polarized array, which works at Ka-band. A hybrid algorithm for electrically large array design is also studied. One kind of patch power divider of high power dividing ratio, which can be satisfied with array weighing method, is designed and calculated. The utilizing of planar sum/difference network in the design reduces the size of antenna effectively. The computation results achieve the desired performance of the antenna, which are also verified by experiment.

articleTitle: Chromosome Recognition as An Effective Algorithm using Polynomial Functional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new approach to the improve chromosome, optimization by means of polynomial functional neural networks is presented. The functional neural networks contain four parameters that need to be optimized, the weight, training parameter, network topology and scaling factor, As a consequence, an accurate comparison with other optimization methods is needed. This paper presents a chromosome that are during the identification by means of optimization algorithm. Experiment result showed that the method is validity.

articleTitle: SAR Interferometry -Novelty in Real Scenario
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A lot of efforts have been put in so far in the InSAR signal processing to develop easier yet accurate methods of generating topographic maps and other products. In order to facilitate better understanding and application of the SAR interferometry, however, there still remain short comings while taking into account certain important factors during various steps. In this paper efforts have been made to encompass all areas in the conventional InSAR signal processing which possess an appropriate reference of relationship with the processing in the real scenario. Methods and relationships have been developed to enable retrieve the accurate results as much as possible. The relevant processing steps have been identified and recommendations have been made to bridge the gaps between the novel and the real InSAR signal processing. The necessary steps involved in processing the received data to the geometrically compensated digital models have been explained in an easy and comprehensible way.

articleTitle: A Cross-Feed Wideband Patch Antenna and Its Hi-Gain Application
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A novel cross-feed wideband patch antenna and its hi-gain application is investigated. The antenna elements are cross-fed by parallel broad brimmed coupled lines to actualize impedance match and enhance gain. Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that the antenna fabricated on a epsiv<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> =2.6 permittivity substrate of h =1 mm thickness can achieve 53% impedance bandwidth (VSWR<2.0) and maximal gain reaches 4.8 dBi, with perfect far-field radiant characteristics and stable phase center. By mounting reflectors and directors around the antenna elements, adjusting parameters, 7-12 dB gain in 51% impedance bandwidth can be achieved. The antenna is easy to design and fabricate. The design parameters can be adjusted easily. The antenna takes on high value in application.

articleTitle: Study of the Millimeter Microstrip Monopulse Antenna Array in the Dual-Sensor System
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The integrated design method of the millimeter-wave (Ka band) microstrip monopulse antenna array and infrared dual-sensor system is presented in this paper. The performance and structure of the sensor are optimized. Meanwhile, the simulated and measured results of the circular planar antenna with a IR aperture are also demonstrated, meanwhile the result improves that the infrared sensor also has effect upon the antenna array.

articleTitle: Full-wave Analysis of Arbitrarily-shaped Groove Guide Resonator
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, arbitrarily-shaped groove guide resonator is analyzed using the method of lines and resonant principle. A novel similar V-shaped groove guide resonator is presented and its resonant performances are numerically calculated and analyzed. The analytic method has virtues such as easy formulation, less computation, universal application and so on.

articleTitle: Series Transmission Line Network Representation of Planar Left-handed Materials
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Recent demonstrations of two dimensional planar Left-handed Materials (LHM) using periodically inductor-capacitor (L-C) loaded transmission Lines, presented by G V. Eleftheriades, Ashwin K. Iyer, and Peter C. Kremer, consist of series impedance Z constituted by capacitors CL and shunt admittance Y constituted by inductors LL (usually formed by vias). In this paper, we propose an alternative representation of planar TL LHM, called series TL LHM. It consists of only series capacitances, series inductors, and no shunt inductors or vias, so it can be more compact and planar, hence easily fabricated. Circuit analysis and full-wave field simulations illustrating its unusual properties, such as the negative refraction and phase compensation of propagating waves, the growth of evanescent waves, are also presented.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling and Ground Effects Compensation in VHF-LB Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The main problems in phased array antenna are mutual coupling and ground effects that destroys the designed radiation pattern. In this paper these undesired effects is compensated over 5 dB for mutual coupling effect and about 10 dB for both mutual coupling and ground effects in wide frequency band 30-88 MHz.

articleTitle: Using noise power spectrality to evaluate the noise and gain behavior of RF receivers
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents and validates a new design method for evaluating the noise and gain behavior of the RF receiver. The proposed technique is based on the noise power spectrality. The noise models for LNA, IF amplifier and mixer are provided to illuminate the detailed design procedure. The validity and efficiency of the proposed design approach has been demonstrated by an ultrashort broadcasting station receiver example and fair agreement has been obtained between the theoretical and simulated results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering from 2D Band-limited Weierstrass Fractal Dielectric Rough Surface Using Kirchhoff Approximation
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A normalized two-dimensional band-limited Weierstrass fractal function is used for modeling the dielectric rough surface. An analytic solution of the scattered field is derived based on Kirchhoff approximation. The variance of scattering intensity is presented to study the fractal characteristics by theoretical analysis and numerical calculations. The important conclusion is obtained that the diffracted envelope slopes of scattering pattern can be approximated to a slope of linear equation. This conclusion will be applicable for solving the inverse problem of reconstructing rough surface and remote sensing.

articleTitle: Multiple Nulls Synthesis for Circular Arrays Using Least Squares Method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents the feasibility of the least squares (LS) based methods in synthesis of multiple nulls in the omnidirectional radiation pattern of circular array antennas. To this purpose, an ideal pattern with an abrupt phase reversal at the angular location of desired nulls is effectively incorporated within the proposed framework. The effects of number of elements and interelement spacing on the characteristics of the radiation pattern are studied. Results demonstrate the presented paradigm provides narrower nulls at the expense of tolerable increment in gain ripple value.

articleTitle: Data Transmission Antennas for Earth Observation Satellites in China
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Since the 1980s, applied satellites and satellite application have been primarily developed in China. The data transmission antennas for Earth Observation Satellites have also been developed during this course, and a few products have been achieved to accommodate to different aspects of demand, especially the new types of data transmission antennas, small in size, are adaptive to small satellites' needs. This paper presents several varieties of data transmission antennas on Earth Observation Satellites of China.

articleTitle: Unit-rate and Low-complexity Space-time Block Coding for Multiple Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Space-time block coding (STBC) has been an effective transmit diversity technique for combating fading due to its orthogonal design, simple decoding and high diversity gains. In this paper, a unit-rate and low-complexity STBC scheme for multiple antennas is proposed, and turbo coding is employed as channel coding to improve the proposed code scheme performance further. Compared with full-diversity multiple antennas STBC schemes, the proposed scheme can implement unit rate, complex orthogonality and partial diversity; and under the same system throughput, it has much smaller computational complexity. Moreover, using the proposed scheme can form efficient spatial interleaving, thus the performance loss due to partial diversity is effectively compensated by the concatenation of turbo coding. Simulation results show that on the condition of the same system throughput and concatenation of turbo coding, the proposed scheme has lower BER than those low-rate and full-diversity multiple antennas STBC schemes.

articleTitle: Extraction of Salient Signal using Optimum Wavelet Receiver
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Wavelet was used as an improvement orthonormal basis to represent signals in the joint time-frequency domain, an architecture of the optimum wavelet based receiver was given. We discussed some issues on the detection of salient signal. We evaluated the performance of the optimum wavelet receiver, it shows optimum in the sense that a specific criterion.

articleTitle: A Wideband E Plane Omnidirectional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A broadband E plane omnidirectional antenna is designed and tested. The antenna measured bandwidth is from 3 GHz to 7 GHz with a VSWR less than 2.2, and from 3 GHz to 5.4 GHz, the variations in the energy level inside its far-field pattern are less than 3 dB. In most of the band, the antenna gain is larger than 0 dBi. All the performance is achieved by using a developed 4 elements T-dipole array.
