articleTitle: Seismoelectric Conversion Wave Propagation in a Fluid-Filled Borehole and Numerical Simulation
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A theoretical borehole model is established to explore the potential application of seismoelectric conversion in well logging. The responses of the borehole fluid, well logging tool and the formation are all considered. The acoustic wave equation, seismoelectric coupling wave governing equation and the electromagnetic wave equation have been solved with the potential function methods in the axial-symmetrical column coordinates system. The converted electric field in the borehole is discussed based on the numerical simulation of a monopole point source with the real axis integral method. A numerical simulation example is presented, and the results show that two kinds of converted electric filed can be recorded without tool consideration, only one the converted electric filed with light speed can be recorded in fluid-filled borehole with tool consideration.

articleTitle: 3D BRDF Statistical Modeling and Optimizing of Various Samples
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A modified and simplified five-parameter model is presented based on the Torrance-Sparrow model. Multi-angle bistatic data of the surfaces of various materials and roughness are fitted by using this model. The results of five-parameter model are in good agreement with the measured data, and closing to the results of two-dimensional bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) models. The five-parameter model shows a good applicability to various surface roughness and different optical materials. The combined algorithm of genetic algorithm and simulated annealing algorithm takes a key role on the salvation of the process of optimization to get the parameters. The five parameters model can be used to construct a 3D BRDF distribution based on the spatial measured data, which may provide more information of light scattering from rough surfaces.

articleTitle: Planar Compact Multiresonator Broadband Microstrip Antenna with Slots loading
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel planar compact multiresonator broadband microstrip antenna was proposed, which includes two slots loading on two rectangular microstrip resonators as the compact units, respectively. The center frequency of the microstrip antenna operates at 2.4 GHz and it has about 5% bandwidth with VSWR<2. Compared to the conventional planar two resonators microstrip antenna, it has the similar impedance bandwidth, but the size reduction is more than 10%. Numerical simulation results demonstrated all above.

articleTitle: The Design of Broadband Planar Array at Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a broadband planar array at Ku band is designed and manufactured, which is comprised of 48times48 annular slot elements. From calculated and experimental results, the obtained impedance bandwidth (VSWR<2) reach 20.56%, the gain reach 34.5 dB. The proposed planar array satisfies the use of satellite communications.

articleTitle: Study on the Scattering Property of the Impedance Terminated Dipole Array by FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The scattering characteristics of the planar array composed of impedance terminated dipoles are studied by finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. The current distribution on the dipoles and the radar cross section (RCS) of the array are obtained and analyzed. It is seen that the array with inductance terminated dipole tends to give lower RCS. Results of this paper are in agreement with those obtained by moment method.

articleTitle: Study on Size Reduction of Quasi-Sierpinski Carpet Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, several novel contracted antenna structures are proposed, in contrast to the conventional Sierpinski carpet microstrip antenna. The novel antenna structures have cross-shaped fractal slots, U-shaped fractal slots and Hilbert slots incorporated into, respectively. In the geometries of these antennas, the 2nd order U-shaped fractal slot, Hilbert slot and cross-shaped fractal slot are embed on the 1st order antenna patch elements, and the 1st order ones on the 2nd patch elements. The effects of slots' width and length on antenna's return loss and resonance frequencies are discussed and their appropriate values are found. These novel slot microstrip antennas can all make the resonance frequencies decrease and reduce the original antenna size effectively. Compared the results with each other, Hilbert slots can reduce the antenna size most obviously.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Alamouti Scheme With Imperfect Multiple Transmit Antennas Selection in Rayleigh Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In a multiple-input-single-output (MISO) communications system, we take the presence of the erroneous channel state information (CSI) into consideration. Multiple transmit antennas selection (TAS) over MISO systems with Alamouti space-time scheme is investigated, and a solution over order statistic characteristic of the selective channel with CSI feedback error is proposed. We assume that channel is an independent and flat Rayleigh fading channel and the system employs binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) modulation. The accurate analytical expressions of bit-error rate (BER) of Alamouti scheme with TAS have been derived. The analysis results show that when the error is existed in CSI we ought to try to choose the subset consisting of largest ordinal number as transmit in a practical system.

articleTitle: Singularity Analysis of the Junction Region for Wire Antenna with Bodies of Revolution
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the singularity in the integrand of electrical field integral equation (EFIE) for the junction region between the wire antenna and the bodies of revolution (BOR) is first analyzed. A method based on suitable changes of coordinates and domains is introduced to extract singularity of self impedance element calculation in junction region and obtain the efficient integral value. Take the wire antenna mounted on a finite solid conducting cylinder as an example, the impedance characteristics and radiation pattern is computation, The good agreement that numerical data obtained using above analysis are compared with those of CST soft shows the method is efficient.

articleTitle: An Accurate Mutual Coupling Calculation For Microstrip Antennas For Impedance Mismatching
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: An exact determination of mutual coupling between microstrip patches is presented in this paper. The classical formula for mutual coupling based on multi-port network theory is popular for determining such coupling. However, this formula ignores the impedance mismatching between antenna and its load. In this presentation an accurate formula for the coupling between patch elements is deduced. For impedance matching case the exact formula reduces to the classical formula. The simulation results show that the consideration of impedance mismatching in mutual coupling calculation is very important.

articleTitle: A study on the Implementation of IEEE1451 for e-Health
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: We're approaching to the Ubiquitous age with development of the internet, recently. The standardization is going to progress in wireless communication. For example, IEEE 802.15.1, IEEE 802.15.4, IEEE 1451. We will refer to IEEE 1451. Attributes of IEEE 1451 are PnP and flexibility and so on. And there is a standard for a e-Health, HL7(Health level seven). HL7 accredited Standards Developing Organizations (SDOs) operating in the healthcare arena. Transducers, defined here as sensors or actuators, serve a wide variety of industry's needs, manufacturing, industrial control, and biomedicine are but a few. This paper we will explain HL7 and IEEE 1451,in briefly. The present time we will realize sensor networking for e- Health using IEEE 1451 standard. For example, in hospital, doctors use sensor. Because, for catch hold of patient's health. In brief, sensor is a STIM and server is aNCAP. So, we will get model for sensor-networking in hospital. We will explain NCAP and STIM more So, this paper will introduce implementation of the IEEE1451.1 and IEEE1451.2. And introduce IEEE1451 and HL7. So we will say that relation between IEE1451 and HL7.

articleTitle: Detection depth of transient electromagnetic method for A-type layer
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: First, the diffusion processt of transient electromagnetic (TEM) field is simulated by FDTD; then the transient field responses on three typical geo-electrical models are obtained with G-S algorithm, and detection depths corresponding observation time are inversed; lastly, the response curves are transformed to time-frequency (T-F) plane by means of Gabor expansion. The results show that conductive overburden of A-type section has retard effect. To detect the same depth requires longer time there exists the overburden. Since electromagnetic energy will concentrate and consume in the overburden, it is necessary to develop high power transmitter to gain sufficient signal noise ratio for explorations in such area. The results have been approved by practical prospecting in Xutuan, Dongpang, Renluo and Xuzhou.

articleTitle: Study on IR detect system effect interval to phased array radar
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the infrared radiation model of phased array radar is studied. And the infrared radiation model of the object is created. The estimated equations of effect interval were given in infrared detect system to phased array radar. As an example, the effect interval in infrared detect system for some or other model phased array radar are appraised calculated aimed at a detector's performance. These results can supply important reference data and theory bastion for the design and emulation of the infrared lead in the related detect system.

articleTitle: The Use of the Reciprocity Theorem for Efficiently Calculating the Far-field of the Cylindrical Conformal Microstrip Arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The main discussion of this paper is a reciprocity approach for calculating the far field of cylindrical conformal microstrip arrays. The first step in the procedure is to solve for the current distribution on the surface of the microstrip patch. The second is to solve for the total field on the surface of the dielectric-coated metallic cylinder produced by a TE- and TM-polarized plane wave. The last step is to approach the far field of the microstrip antenna by the reciprocity theorem. The major advantage of this method is that it does not require the tedious evaluation of complicated media Dyadic Green's function for curved geometries in the evaluation of the far fields. The agreement between the results of calculated and measured is very good.

articleTitle: The effects of near-field factors on rectangular horn antenna's phase center
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A study of the effects of near filed factors on rectangular horn antenna's phase center has been carried out by using finite integration technique and finite element method. The exact phase center of the horn antenna has been solved by adjusting the position of initial phase center using iterative method in the software HFSS. The effect of the infrared detector simulator which is constituted by lamp, line and media board, placed in the horn antenna on phase center is analyzed further more. Indeed the result is beneficial to the design of horn antenna's phase center and it can instruct the actual analysis of near field factors.

articleTitle: Performance and Design of Double Coaxial Stepped Impedance Resonators for Mobile Communication
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: An improved accurate model for stepped impedance resonators with a double coaxial structure (DC-SIRs) is proposed in this paper. The step discontinuities of the DC-SIRs have been fully considered in the model. The resonance frequency calculated by the improved accurate model agrees well with the measured results. The band-pass filters have been designed using the accurate model of DC-SIRs and show excellent performances such as more compact size, lower insertion loss and it can be used for lower frequencies.

articleTitle: Monostatic microwave imaging of arbitrary convex PEC cylinder
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Monostatic approach to 2D microwave imaging is proposed, in which the global optimization method is served as solver and the signal pre-processing is used to estimate the sparse size of unknown object and to determine the range of parameters for optimization method. By comparing efficiency of MGA with that of GA Two test examples are presented and the optimized results are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Procedure of Computation of Local Phase Center Position and Analysis of Its Displacement for Antennas with Elliptical Polarization Radiation
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A procedure for the computation of position of local phase center of thin-wire helical antenna is suggested. The procedure is based on the analysis of the antenna phase characteristics in an arbitrary point of space. The results of local phase center position displacement analysis are presented. The coordinates of the observation point, the frequency of the exciting current and geometry of the antenna were considered as factors affecting the position of the local phase center.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis of the Mushroom-like EBG Structure Based on a Quasi-static New Model
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Based on a quasi-static new model, the relations between structure parameters and resonance frequency are analyzed in detail. At the same time, a precision comparison is performed among the new model formulas, Sievenpiper model formulas and Yang modified formulas. The results show that, the theory value of new model compared with other two model values is the closest to the simulation value, and there are some new understanding on the effect of gap width and visa radius. According to the new model and analyzed results, some engineering design guidelines for the mushroom-like EBG structures are presented.

articleTitle: A New Miniaturized Electronically Tunable Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper a new electronically tunable band pass filter using coupled ring resonator is described. This filter can tune frequency ranges from 2 GHz to 4 GHz. In comparison with designed filter by Y.H.SHu the size of this filter reduced about 69% with the same frequency performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Printed Dual Band Antenna Structure Operating at UMTS and HIPERLAN2 Bands: Narrow CPW-fed Sleeve Monopole
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: By using of a new coplanar waveguide feeding (CPW feeding) technique to a planar sleeve monopole, a narrow width antenna with uniplanar structure is proposed for dual band operation at UMTS (1.885-2.200 GHz) and HIPERLAN2 (5.470- 5.725 GHz) bands. Proposed antenna has considerable narrow width (width of 7.8 mm) and simple structure. The antenna radiation pattern is almost as the radiation pattern of a monopole antenna and the gain remains nearly constant within UMTS and HIPERLAN2 bands. The antenna is suitable for application to wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Study and Simulation on Bistatic SAR
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: After introduction of system configuration of a multi-static SAR, essential principle and system performance is analyzed. By utilizing the Versatile SAR Simulation Model (VSARSM) simulation results are given, which sustained the theory.

articleTitle: Load Resistance Value Changes Affect on the Plane Log-periodic Dipole Printed Antenna Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The paper mainly use Ansoft HFSS electromagnetic field simulation software for the simulation of simple plane log-periodic dipole printed antennas, focused on whether the changes of the far-end loading resistor value impact on such antenna radiation characteristics, using wires patches ~ a feature theoretical calculations of a few approximate phase center equivalent methods. The certification of the accuracy of the approximate calculation has been completed for plane log-periodic dipole antennas added terminals load resistance. At the same time, the paper has discussed the various value of the resistance whether to affect on the horizontal and vertical phase center.

articleTitle: A Time-Gating-Based Method for Correcting Phase Errors Caused by Cable Flexing in Planar Near-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new method based on time-gating technique for correcting phase errors caused by flexing cable is introduced, which can be used in planar near-field test systems. It was shown by simulation and experiments that this method is valid on X band and could be easily put into practice.

articleTitle: S-Domain Modeling of Rectangular Waveguide with Dielectric Inset (3D case)
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: We introduce a new method for the determination of the generalized admittance matrix of a rectangular waveguide section loaded with a dielectric inset of arbitrary shape. A state space - integral equation approach is applied which leads to the pole expansion of the admittance matrix in the s-domain.

articleTitle: Analysis of Phase Synchronization Errors Based on Distributed Small Satellite SAR System
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Phase synchronization between transmitters and receivers caused by the separation between transmitters and receivers is a key technique to distributed small satellite SAR (DSS-SAR) systems. The effects of phase synchronization errors on pulse compression and imaging will be analyzed in this paper and it is validated by the computer simulation, thus provides the bases for the parameters setting and phase compensation on the theory.

articleTitle: Measurements of Complex Permittivity Using Dielectric Resonator at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In order to investigate the characteristic of single crystal and polycrystalline ceramics at millimeter-wave frequencies, a method for measuring low-loss dielectric materials has been developed. Using a dielectric rod resonator excited by a dielectric waveguide, effective conductivity of conducting plates for short circuiting the resonator is determined. The complex permittivity of the dielectric rod is determined by the resonant frequency and unloaded quality factor of the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0ml</sub>-mode resonator. Then the complex permittivities of single crystal sapphire, polycrystalline ceramics, and cordierite have been obtained at 60 GHz. Finally, for all the specimens measured in this paper, the proposed method is seen to provide much better accuracy for values.

articleTitle: Novel Dual-Mode Microstrip Bandpass Filters Using Fractal-Shaped Triangular Patch Resonators
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, two types of bandpass filters using fractal-shaped triangular resonators are proposed, and their filter performances are simulated and optimized. By using etched fractal-shaped defected structures in the triangular patch resonators, both of the filters have compact sizes, high selectivity and simple structures. The effects of parameters variation for the fractal-shaped structures are also studied. Measured results of the filter using three fractal-shaped structures are in good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Study of the Improved MM-Wave Omni-directional Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Microstrip antennas possess some attractive features such as low profile, light weight, small volume and low production cost. Meanwhile, most conventional mm-wave omni-directional antennas use waveguide or dielectric antennas which have some shortcomings comparing with microstrip antennas. An improved mm-wave omni-directional microstrip antenna is presented in this paper. Two directors are added beside an open-circuit terminal microstrip line. Therefore, the antenna shows better omni-directional performance. The simulated and measured results are demonstrated and discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of the Metal Shield on the Calibration Accuracy of a Microwave Calibration Load
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In calibrating a microwave radiometer, the calibration load (the blackbody) is usually equipped with a metal shield. Due to the imperfect conductivity of the metal used, the shield will influence the calibration accuracy. In this paper, a physical model is constructed base on the radiation transfer theory to study the effect of the metal shield on the calibration accuracy. Simulation results show that the influence of the metal shield can be up to a few tenths of Kelvin, depending on the metal type, the shield an the antenna size.

articleTitle: An Improved ESPRIT-like Algorithm for Coherent Signal and Its Application for 2-D DOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for coherent signal is always an important aspect, because it will cause rank loss of the spatial covariance matrix. The conventional solution is to use smoothing algorithm, but recently a new technique is proposed, which reconstructs the spatial covariance matrix in Toeplitz pattern and no longer be affected by coherency. In this paper, an improved algorithm based the new technique is proposed, which can reduce the computational burden. Finally, a 2-D coherent DOA estimation method using 3-aixs crossed array is suggested. Simulation results are presented to verify the efficacy.

articleTitle: A Novel Source Number Estimator Without Eigendecomposition
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we present another source number estimator without the necessary eigendecomposition, it is based on the Lanczos process and Sturm algorithm and Finally, we provide a simulated data example to evaluate the proposed estimator.

articleTitle: A New Kind of Optical Notch Filters in Photonic Crystals Using Cavities with Open Structure
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Notch filters in photonic crystal (PC) structures play an important role in designing integrated photonic circuits. One way to making such filters is cavity waveguide coupling in PC structures. In this work, we introduce a new kind of such filters that contains cavities with open structure.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Crosstalk Penalty in 2.5GB/s and 10GB/S Serial optical modules
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic crosstalk poses a serious problem in advanced serial communication modules. This paper focuses on the primary sources of crosstalk penalty in a 2.5 Gb/s optic transceiver and a 10Gb/s optic transponder. A novel method to quantify the crosstalk penalty by observing a receiver's bit-error-ratio (BER) versus transmitter to receiver signal phase is proposed. A coupled microstrip transmission line model is also explored to demonstrate inductive crosstalk coupling.

articleTitle: The Analytical Solution for the Transmembrane Potential Induced on a Cell Membrane in Suspensions Exposed to Microwaves at Frequency Between 100MHz and 20GH
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a second order analytical model of transmembrane potential (TMP) on the cells in suspensions exposed to microwaves in 100 MHz to 20 GHz frequency range, was derived. During the exposure of a microwave in this range, the conductivity of a cell membrane increase dramatically. So it has to be considered during the derivation of the TMP. The second order analytical model shows that the TMP on a cell in suspensions depends on the frequency and amplitude of the external field, cell arrangement, cell value fraction, conductivity of the cytoplasm, membrane and medium.

articleTitle: Accurate and Efficient Analysis of Aperture Coupled Cylindrically Conformal Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A full wave method is proposed to analyze the characteristics of the aperture coupled cylindrically conformal microstrip antennas. The near field of the antenna is obtained through conformal FDTD method in cylindrical coordinates and then the equivalence and duality theorems combined with the modified spectral domain dyadic Green's functions for cylindrically stratified media are used to calculate the radiation patterns. As well, a broadband antenna of this type with stacked structure is realized.

articleTitle: System Electromagnetic Compatibility Forecast Methods Based on Reliability theory
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Through analyzing the definition, development process, forecast indicators and the forecast methods between system reliability and electromagnetic compatibility of system, this paper point that it can be consulted between electromagnetic compatibility of system forecast and system reliability. This paper put forward electromagnetic compatibility of system forecast method based on system reliability theory.

articleTitle: A Study Of Air Target Detection Base On Signal Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper introduces an allocation method for air target detection based on DBS TV satellite signal non-cooperation space-ground bistatic (multi) radar and analyses its fundamental principle. Upon the plenitude study of the characteristic of target information acquisition and information processing of bistatic radar, this paper puts forward a kind of target information acquisition technique that is different from the typical bistatic radar system. Basic principle for target detection and target information acquisition is analyzed.

articleTitle: A Survey of Research Method of High-Speed Interconnect for Signal Integrity
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In the paper, conception and sorts of high-speed interconnect for signal integrity was introduced; methods for circuit analysis and electromagnetic analysis of high-speed interconnection as important parts were also studied. The two methods based on telegraph equations, modified nodal admittance (MNA) and MAXWELL equations of electromagnetic use value method for calculation or simulate for corresponding circuit models. Expatiation of both methods was accomplished in the paper. In addition, model-order reduction arithmetic for large-scale circuit was discussed.

articleTitle: An Imaging Simulation Method of SAR for Three-dimensional Targets
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The imaging simulation of SAR (synthetic aperture radar) is very useful for designing and understanding SAR systems. In this paper, a fast image simulating algorithm of SAR for complex three-dimensional ground object targets is presented. The simulation parameters and echo signal expression of SAR system are presented. In the simulation testing, the imaging of a complex three-dimensional ground object target is realized.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Space-Filling-Based Slot Antenna for 2.4/5.2 GHz Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper a reconfigurable microstrip-fed slot antenna for 2.4/5.2 GHz band applications is proposed. The design of these slots that form several "island-like" metal blocks in the ground are based on the use of space-filling curves, which endow the antenna with broadband performance, and here some modifications are implemented. By connecting several "islands" with some circuits to build bridge between them, the radiation properties can be changed, including the resonant frequency and radiation patterns. Here, a switch is added to achieve a reconfigurable antenna, and with the switch state changing, the radiation properties can be altered. The antenna structure proposed could be reconstructed in several manners, and in this paper, we give an easy way to realize the frequency hopping for 2.4/5.2 GHz band systems. The design and analysis for this antenna are accomplished by using HFSS (high frequency structure simulator), and its performance is calculated. Then the antenna prototype is fabricated and measured, the calculated and measured results show good agreements, which implies that such a type of antennas can achieve our design requirements.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Crank-Shape Feed-Line
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a new method for broadening of impedance bandwidth of rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has been demonstrated. In the proposed configuration, two adjacent resonant modes were excited by the additional L-shape feed-line. For the suggested optimum feed network, the impedance bandwidth of over than 11% and 24.5% (for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> > 10 dB) are obtained in two separate frequency bands at 5-8 GHz.

articleTitle: Fast Ray Tracing Propagation Prediction Model For Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A fast brute force ray tracing method employed to analyze indoor radio communication environment. To speed up the numerical calculation, several improved techniques are applied. The achieved overall enhancement, measured by verification of obtained results for three indoor case studies. Significant improvements observed in terms of calculation time and estimated field strength values have good agreement with recorded measurements.

articleTitle: Compact and Broadband Dielectric Resonator Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A novel wide band Dielectric Resonator Antenna with reduced size, suitable for WLAN applications, is reported. The high permittivity dielectric resonator is excited by two microstrip line in E-plane and a vertical metal plate is placed inside the DR to improve the bandwidth. This configuration exhibits a bandwidth of 26.9% and nearly omni-directional radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Amendment of Cavity Perturbation Technique for Loss Tangent Measurement at Microwave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Theoretically, the quality factor of a metal resonant cavity will be increased after introducing a lossless dielectric sample. However, for the conventional cavity perturbation method, widely used on the measurements of microwave dielectric properties, this increment of quality factor is not put into the consideration of calculation on loss tangent measurement. Therefore, the conventional resonant perturbation formulae for dielectric loss measurement should be amended. This amendment is introduced in this study and the measuring error on loss tangent on the conventional formula is discussed. Experiments have shown the improvement of measurement accuracy by this modification.

articleTitle: A New Absorbing Boundary Condition for FEMTD
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The measured equation of invariance method in time domain (TD-MEI) is modified to adapt for the finite element method in time domain (FEMTD), it is applied to terminate the computation domain. The radiation problem of a line source is solved by using this scheme, the numerical results is presented and the validity and the accuracy are discussed.

articleTitle: A Fast DOA Estimation Algorithm Based on Direct Data Domain Least Square Approach
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new fast direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm based on direct data domain least square (D3LS) approach is presented. The matrix equation, which is formed according to the idea of D3LS, is solved via the conjugate gradient (CG) method to get the weight vector from different look direction. Then, the output power from each look direction and the directional spectrum is obtained. Finally, with a rough estimation by output power and a fine estimation by directional spectrum, the DOAs of incident signals are determined. As a different algorithm from conventional ones such as MUSIC, it processes very few data snapshots with no use for the formation of the sample covariance matrix and matrix inversion operation. Therefore, it may be so effective in real-time application. In addition, the proposed algorithm is also available for the DOAs estimation of coherent signals. The estimation capability is proved by simulation results.

articleTitle: Speech Source 3D Localization Focusing Algorithms Based on Microphone Array
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: To classical wideband focusing DOA estimation algorithm, an initial estimate of the DOA's and several iterations are required, and the performance of real time is bad. A speech source 3D localization algorithm based on wideband focusing theory is presented in this paper, and it doesn't require initial estimations and iterations. The optimal criterion of this algorithm is the MMSE, i.e. the minimized mean square error of the correlation matrix of focused frequency and the others. This algorithm has the advantage of the low computational complexity for the real-time applications. Simulation results show the high performance of the 3D localization estimation is obtained when the proposed algorithm is used in planar uniform circle array.

articleTitle: An Novel Design for an Ultra-wide Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Narrowband antennas are not suitable for UWB systems. This paper emphasizes on the design for mono-cone and sphere-loaded mono-cone antennas. The voltage standing wave ratio (VWSR), input impedance, fidelity coefficient of radiated pulse, radiant efficiency and radiant patterns are computer calculated. Simulated results confirm that the mono-cone and sphere-loaded mono-cone antennas be of good ultra-wide band performance. Sphere-loaded mono-cone antennas are better to radiate ultra-wide band pulses than mono-cone antennas on condition of the same size of antennas.

articleTitle: A study of recovery method for radio interference on backscatter ionogram
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: An image recovery method based on adaptive wavelet filter, DCT filter and iterated denoising, is introduced into the recovery of radio interference on backscatter ionogram. The algorithm is testified by ionogram of Australia, and PSNR of this method is up to the order of 40 dB. The method in this paper has advantages over traditional method, and a better statistical performance is obtained for backscatter data of research center of Hongmen. In addition, the wavelet method have a better edge effect and ability of keeping structure, which is a important target of auto scaling of backscatter ionogram.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Microstrip Stepped Impedance Lowpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Design of a stepped impedance microstrip low pass filter is proposed here, with improved performances. The result of the filter shows accurate attenuation at the cut-off frequency.

articleTitle: Application of Adaptive Interference Cancellation in EMC Tests
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper will introduce a scheme adopting adaptive interference cancellation to eliminate background noise in EMC tests. The principle is explained and an example is given to illuminate that the effect is excellent. This offers an available method to carry out EMC tests, such as RE and RS, without anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Cassegrain antenna system based on free-space laser communication
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Antenna, which whether transmits or receives correct signal or not is our main care and our direction, is an important part in any communication systems. Because of the characteristics of laser different from radio, the antenna system of point-to-point laser communication system must be designed strictly. In this paper, we mainly study the optical antenna in the space communication. We describe the optical antenna's structure. The performances of optical antenna are first given in this paper.

Author Keywords: Cassegrain antenna system free-space laser communic ation

articleTitle: Numerical Computation of the Green's Function of a Layered Media With Rough Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A method in order to obtain the Green's function of a layered media containing rough interfaces is addressed. The method is based on the assumption that the perturbations of the rough surfaces from the planar ones are objects buried in a layered media with planar interfaces. Applications to some scattering problems show that the Green's function obtained through the proposed method can be effectively used for locally rough surfaces.

articleTitle: Compact coplanar waveguide low-pass filter using a novel electromagnetic bandgap structure
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In the present paper, a new electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure is proposed to design and fabricate low-pass filters on coplanar waveguide (CPW). Using the novel EBG structure, the filter prototypes exhibit sharp cutoff and low insertion loss in the passband. An equivalent lumped L-C circuit mode is introduced to describe the proposed EBG structure, which manifests an elliptic-function low-pass frequency response. Using only three units of this novel EBG cell, a compact low-pass filter device has been fabricated, which achieved sharp cutoff and deep attenuation levels on the stop band. The measured results showed consistency with the simulation using the method of momentum (MoM).

articleTitle: EMC Design Technologies on EW Weapons and Equipment
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A novel method named "top-down, systemic, quantificational pre-design" is investigated to resolve the disadvantages of the traditional electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design method on electronic warfare (EW) weapons and equipment. As design scheme of EW weapons and equipment is conceived, systemic energy-transmission models and interference relationship matrices are devised. Then the security of receivers and other receptors is analyzed with the method of numerical simulation, behavioral simulation, equivalent calculation, statistics of datum, etc. The perfect system EMC performance can be achieved by evaluating EMC performance, distributing the EMC parameters quantification ally, optimizing design time after time. Additionally, the system EMC performance can be analyzed along with the change of subsystem parameters. The subsystem parameters can be adjusted to meet the system EMC performance as well. The potential EMC problems can be exposed at the stage of design and resolved before the design is finalized. It has been applied in EMC design on a number of EW weapons and equipment with a high success rate, and offered important technical support for resolving the acute EMC problems in research and development of models.

articleTitle: A New Approach of Target Identification Using Enhanced Radar Range Profiles
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Due to the aspect dependence of high resolution range profiles (HRRPs), traditional radar HRRPs target identification (ID) methods usually use averaged or weighted HRRPs as an aspect template. A major shortcoming is that HRRPs cannot provide information about target's cross-range. In this study, we present an application of statistics method on complex radar targets. The enhanced HRRPs extracted by this method were used in radar target identification. It is shown from simulation results that identification performance can be improved greatly by using the enhanced HRRPs features combined with a two-stage fuzzy classifier.

articleTitle: Fast Electromagnetic Modeling and Imaging Simulation of Spacecraft by Ground Based ISAR
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Ground based ISAR has its distinctive advantage for imaging spacecraft in orbit. In order to simulate real radar used for imaging an orbiting spacecraft, this paper applies the Physical Optics (PO) method, which is a high frequency approximation algorithm to calculate the radar echo of complex targets. Based on the simulated scattering data for a range of frequencies and a range of aspect angles, a standard 2D imaging algorithm is applied to generate radar image. In this paper, two cases of imaging geometry are introduced: (1) the ground radar is in the orbital plane of the object; (2) the radar is not in the orbital plane. Equivalent translational and rotational moving model is derived. And the Chinese Shenzhou spacecraft is taken as an example for presenting the simulation result.

articleTitle: Compact CPW-to Microstrip transition design for MMIC packaging
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In MMIC circuit design, the transitions and interconnects are essential components for integration and packaging [1-3]. However, the conventional distributed type transition circuits will result in great loss owing to their huge size, most especially in medium and low frequency band. In this paper, a new CPW-to-microstrip transition design based on lumped element circuits is proposed. The optimized design can achieve a return loss of less than 10 dB from 3 to 14 GHz and insertion loss of less than ldB from 3 to 14 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of Millimeter Wave Y-Junction Microstrip Circulator
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: FEM (finite element method) based on the weak form of Helmholtz equation is first here employed to deal with the inhomogeneous structure, shielded Y-junction microstrip circulator at millimeter-wave band. The scattering parameters of the circulator are computed in two steps. As a first step, the field distribution in the shielded microstrip is calculated in the two-dimensional (2-D) FEM. In second step, the three-dimensional (3-D) Vector-FEM is used to model the inhomogeneous structure of the circulator, and FEM field are matched with the field of microstrip at the 3 interfaces. So a sparse matrix equation is obtained, and it is solved with the SSOR-BICG algorithm. Numerical results of the circulator are presented and compared when the ferrite disk radius changed. Also, the electric field distribution in the ferrite disk is depicted to show the circulating process.

articleTitle: Polarimetric Radar Pulse Echoes from Lunar Regolith Layer with Scatter Inhomogeneity and Rough Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: To explore the potential utilities of lower frequency (L band) radar pulse for lunar exploration, a theoretical model of stratified lunar regolith media and numerical simulation of polarimetric radar pulse echoes are developed. The lunar regolith layer consists of the low lossy regolith layer with randomly rough top and bottom interfaces, and a layer of random stone-scatterers (spatially oriented oblate spheroids are assumed) is embedded and overlays the underlying rock media. The time domain Mueller matrix solution is derived to take account for scattering mechanisms of the stratified scatter media. Temporal characteristics and structure of the polarimetric echo profile as functional dependence on model parameters such as the layer thickness and the content of FeO+TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, are numerically simulated, and well display an image of regolith structures. It demonstrates a potential new way to explore moon surface in future.

articleTitle: Comparison Study on Single-layered and Double-layered Differential Symmetric Circular Spiral Inductors
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Based on the Ansoft 3D electromagnetic field software HFSS and the typical lumped equivalent-circuit model of spiral inductors on silicon (SIOS) for RF integrated circuits (RFICs), the comparison study of single-layered and double-layered differential symmetric circular spiral inductors has been given. The numerical analyses showed that the former can give better results of quality factor (QF) and self-resonant frequency (SRF) and the L value of the former can satisfied the nH level requirements where the Q factor obtains its highest value. Experimental results showed that the former can gives a 50.5% increase for the maximum Q value and 164.5% increase for the SRF whereas the latter can supply over 3 times larger L value. The simulation results have good agreements with the theoretical analyses. At last the design guidelines were given according to the simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Broadband circularly polarized square microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The design of a broadband square microstrip antenna with circular polarization radiation is presented in this paper. The antenna comprises a thick air substrate and single square microstrip radiating patch, which is excited by dual capacitive-coupled feed disks connected to a Wilkinson power divider having equal amplitude and a 90deg phase shift between its two outputs. The experimental results show that the proposed antenna is able to achieve an impedance bandwidth of 69% for VSWR less than 2 and a 3 dB axial-ratio bandwidth about 23%.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Method for Analyzing Isolation between Antennas on an Electrically Large Metallic Surface
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the problem of calculating the isolation between antennas on a perfectly conducting circular cylinder is considered. The isolation is calculated by a hybrid MoM - UTD technique. It is impractical to calculate the isolation between antennas influenced by the electrically large system only by using the method of moment (MoM) because such method consumes too much memory and computing resources. On the other hand, the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD), though providing a popular solution to process electrically large objects, is an asymptotic method that cannot deliver a computing accuracy as high as MoM method. The combination of MoM and UTD takes the advantages of both methods and efficiently solves the problem of an electrically large object. The isolation between wire antennas is computed with the influence of the electrically large cylindrical surface being considered and sweep-frequency results are obtained, which cannot be delivered by MoM.

articleTitle: A New Method to Calculate the Theoretical Value of the NSA
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: this paper simply introduces the traditional calculation method of the normalized site attenuation (NSA) of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) test site, and also analyzes some errors of the traditional method. Then based on the theory discussed above, a new method to calculate the theoretical value of the NSA is put forward. The new method has more universality than the traditional one.

articleTitle: The Transmembrane Potential Induced on a Permeabilized Cell in SuspensionsExposed to DC Pulse Fields
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: During the electroporation, the membrane conductivity increase dramatically. The transmembrane potential (TMP) on the permeabilize cells in suspensions exposed to a DC pulse field, is theoretically a complex problem especially due to the rotation and the mutual interactions among the permeabilize cells. Based on the Maxwell equivalent theory, an analytical solution for the TMP on the permeabilize cells was derived in this paper. The equation shows that the TMP depends on parameters such as the external electric field, critical angle of electroporation, cell radio, conductivity of the cytoplasm, membrane and external medium, cell arrangement and cell volume fraction.

articleTitle: Design for Thermally Stable Multi-finger Power SiGe HBTs Using Finger Length-and Space-adjusted Methods
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: For power bipolar transistors, the emitter-ballasting-resistor is usually used to improve the thermal stability. However, the ballasting-resistor degrades the output power, power gain, power-added efficiency (PAE) of the transistor. In this paper, the thermal stability can be improved substantially by adjusting either the spacing or length of the emitter fingers without using ballasting resistors. The temperature rise at the device center of the space-adjusted HBT is suppressed by reducing heat flow from adjacent fingers, and that of the length-adjusted HBT is suppressed by reducing heat generation in the region.

articleTitle: ASLC Based on Phased Array under Saturated Attack
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the adaptive side-lobe canceller (ASLC) under saturated attack will be analyzed; especially the ASLC based on the phased array is concerned. The mathematic model of weights equation and cancellation ratio (CR) under saturated attacks is presented. Finally the simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: The High-Mode-Merging Technique for Dielectric Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The mode-matching method and transverse resonance technique for dielectric waveguide was developed in 60s-70s last century. After that, only few attentions were paid. But it may be an effective method. According to the strict mode-matching method of the solving electromagnetic field, a derived method-high-mode-merging method is approached, than a kind of the equivalent network can be got. The network not only expresses the characteristic of the dominant mode mainly but also considers the influence of high modes if they are excited. Thus it guarantees strictness of original theory and simplifies the calculation consumedly.

articleTitle: Simulating Photonic Bandgap Antennas on Silicon Substrate
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: With the idea of having antennas on chip, this paper describes an implementation of a micro antenna fabricated on a silicon substrate in order to have uniformity in fabrication steps that will help bring down cost of manufacturing and efficiency of design. We have also looked into the field of photonic or electromagnetic bandgap (PBG/EBG) structures to increase the efficiency of the antenna by reducing the material loss and prevent surface waves to travel through the substrate.

articleTitle: A New Channel Tracking Algorithm Based on Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Multipath is a major impairment in the wireless communication system, and the channel estimation significantly affects the performance of the receiver. Its performance can be improved if an appropriate channel estimation filter is used according to the foreknow information of the fading channel. We propose an algorithm which uses the Kalman filter based on Clarke's model to track the time-varying multipath fading channel. To reduce the complexity of the high-dimensional Kalman filter for channel estimation of the paths, we use a low-dimensional Kalman filter for the estimation of each path. We investigate into how to estimate the channel by the Kalman filter in the pilot-aided wirelesss system. Simulations show this algorithm is effective for the estimation of the fading channel when the performance of the channel estimation is presented in terms of the mean-square error(MSE).

articleTitle: The Diagnoses System for Performance of Absorbing Materials on Large Target
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new method measuring and diagnosing the performance of absorbing materials on a large target is presented. Then a system based on the method was created. The measuring results of cones which are partially covered with absorbing materials indicate that the system is suitable for prompt and complete testing performance of absorbing materials on a large target.

articleTitle: An Approach to the Dyadic Green's Functions for a Rectangular Chirowaveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A novel method of formulating eigenfunction expansion of the dyadic Green's function in lossless, recipcocal and homogeneous chirowaveguides is given,using this method, the non-divergence vector potential equation can be transformed into that similar to achiral media,the corresponding wavefield decomposition is used to obtain the vector wave function. A specific application to the analytic solution of electromagnetic wave propagation in a rectangular chirowaveguide illustrates the method.

articleTitle: The Controlling for Reflected Wave's Phase with Active Periodical Structure
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Active control of reflected wave phase is present in this paper. Using the periodical surface's character of band gap and impedance transition of electromagnetic crystal structure such as PBG, FSS and HIS, and so on, put the varactor diode onto the approximate HIS to join each cell of metal on top layer to realize the electronic control for periodical structure, will establish the active periodical structure and effect the propagation characteristic of incident electromagnetic wave and realize controlling the phase of reflected wave. The simulation test prove that this method and technology could control reflected wave's phase by using single or double layer active periodical structure effectively.

articleTitle: Polarimetric Analysis of Radar Signature of a Manmade Structure
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Identification of manmade structures from radar images has always been a difficult task, especially for single-polarization radar. Fully polarimetric radar, however, can provide detailed information on scattering mechanisms that could enable the target or the structure to be identified. Complexity remains stemming from overlaps of single bounce scattering, double bounce scattering and triple and higher order bounce scattering from various components of manmade structure that makes physical interpretation a challenge. In this paper, we will present an interesting example using polarimetric SAR data of the Great Belt Bridge, Denmark, to illustrate the capability of polarimetric SAR in analyzing radar signatures. Polarimetric target decomposition is used to differentiate the multiple bounce scattering contributions contained in the polarimetric SAR images. Two C-band Danish EMISAR data takes, the first obtained during the bridge's construction and the second after its completion, are used to extract the scattering characteristics of the bridge deck, bridge cables and supporting structures.

articleTitle: Ad-hoc routing Protocol-based Ubiquitous Network System In the Hospital Environment
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: AODV is one of the various routing protocol on ad-hoc networks. This paper analyzes information about the user who moves from among the multi techniques which composes the ubiquitous environment, and proposes about the network configuration and management to execute ubiquitous system. In this paper, we propose efficient method that has AODV protocol advantage and the property of power efficiency and reliable data transmission in the hospital or home environment. Our proposed method uses the mobile nodes which have the sensor and the role and an operational process of each system configuration is described in this paper.

articleTitle: Numerical and Experimental Analysis of Linear-End Wire Bow-tie Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper the properties of the transmitting waveforms and the footprints with the linear-end wire bow-tie antenna are measured and simulated by the FDTD method. The results of the simulations and the measurements are contrasted. The two types of results are in basic agreement. These results are beneficial to the deep studies about the linear-end wire bow-tie antennas.

articleTitle: On Dyadic Green's Function of a Field Vector
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A method of deriving directly the irrotational and non-divergence component for the spectral domain dyadic Green's function of a field vector is given. Helmholtz theorem and the irrotational and non-divergence splitting of dyadic Dirac delta function are used to obtain the irrotational and non-divergence dyadic Green's function, a specific application to the electromagnetic wave field in chiral media illustrates the method.

articleTitle: The Study ofASF Prediction Method in Irregular-Terrain
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: As the potential of Loran-C in land vehicle tracking, and in marine and aeronautical navigation explored, the importance of employing accurate values of additional secondary factors (ASFs) is increasingly being recognized. A computer method that used to generate ASFs for irregular terrain is developed. In order to determine the prediction accuracy of the method in irregular terrain, during the summer of 2005, a series of tests were conducted in the selected area in Jiangxi Province. Using the set of ASF values obtained by the method above, the time delay correction errors of ground-wave propagation are reduced to less than 200 ns in the land.

articleTitle: Real-Time Display of Faculas in the FSO Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The main disadvantage of free space optical (FSO) systems is the disturbing role played by the atmosphere on light propagation. This paper studies the faculas which is the most intuitionistic way through the atmospheric channel. The faculas reflect the condition of the receiver actually. Because the research of some references mainly From simulation, we know that the turbulence is described by faculas perfectly and fog and rain are described by attenuation.

articleTitle: Proposal of a novel punctured LDPC coding scheme for Ultra Wide Band system
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: As a new spread spectrum system, an ultra wide band technology has attracted much attention in high speed indoor multiple access radio communications. An UWB communication system with channel coding is noticing for avoiding the performance degradation due to adverse channel propagation conditions. In this paper, we propose a novel punctured low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding scheme for UWB systems. Differently from the conventional puncture coding, we puncture the pulses after the UWB system repeating the LDPC coded bits. From our analysis and numerical results, we find this new scheme give a significant performance gain compared with the conventional scheme. Furthermore, the receiver construction is simpler since the puncture position information is not needed.

articleTitle: Analysis and synthesis of a multi-arm conical spiral antenna to form shaped-conical radiation patterns
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A multi-arm conical spiral wire antenna used in low orbit satellite communications is proposed, which can form cardio or conical patterns by adjusting its geometrical parameters. It has better polarization characteristic than the two-arm spiral antenna proposed in the reference. With the increase of its height and spiral constant its beam deviation from the axis increase while its power gain decrease to form conical radiation patterns. Several graphs about the influence of the parameters on radiation patterns are presented in this paper for the optimization of the antenna.

articleTitle: Application of the Self-Metron Method to first order MEI-ABC
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: When the MEI coefficients are found by traditional method, the accuracy of 5-points or 7-points are not better, and even worse than that of the 3-points[1]. The results are very depressing. However, this paper expend the 3-points Self-Metron Method, and discuss 5-points and 7-points. The simulation results show that the accuracy of the 7-points is much better than 3-points, 5-points and traditional method. The advantage of 7-points could not be replaced by 3-points or 5-points.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Ship Detection in SAR Imagery Based on Convolution between Different Polarization Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new approach is proposed for ship detection with SAR (Synthetics Aperture Radar) images based on the convolution between different polarimetric channels. The method takes advantages of different statistical behaviors among ships and surrounding ocean, interpreting the information through the convolution in order to provide a more reliable detection. The simulations show that the convolution is sensitive to the size and shape of ships not to sea state. The method can be used under high sea state and have no relation to the movement of ships. Moreover, the method is general which is not only suitable for dual polarization data but also for full polarization data. The detection performance over both simulated and real images confirms the robustness of the method.

articleTitle: A New Way of Ultra Wideband Analog Signal Reconstruction in the Optical Sensor for Pulsed Electromagnetic Measurement
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A new way for ultra wideband (UWB) analogy signal high accuracy reconstruction based on intersection and shift of frequency spectrum is proposed. This method effectively solves the problem of direct A/D conversion of the UWB signals up to several GHz. The scheme is given and the simulation is made. The simulation results verify the good performance of the reconstruction scheme.

articleTitle: An Approach Based on Normalization Processing for Two-Dimensional Subarray Level ADBF
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Adaptive digital beamforming (ADBF) at subarray level has important applications in phased array radar systems. This paper studies two-dimensional ADBF methods at subarray level. We present the signal model of two-dimension ADBF at subarray level. Generalizing ADBF applied to one-dimension linear array to phased array at subarray level, we can obtain two-dimension ADBF at subarray level, but its limitation is that adaptive processing makes the SLL (sidelobe level) of the pattern increase remarkably. Therefore, we present two-dimensional ADBF at subarray level based on normalization. This method can obtain adaptive pattern the same as quiescent pattern for the case of absence of jammer and non-overlapped subarrays, while improve the SLL of the adaptive pattern remarkably in presence of jammers. Simulation results indicate the validity of the introduced method.

articleTitle: A New Method of Radar Imaging Bases on GRECO
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) is a way of radar imaging, but the recognition of this way is not very well. This paper presents a different way of radar imaging, which bases on GRECO. This paper compares the two ways, and the conclusion is that the new way is better than the ISAR imaging in shape of its recognition, and new way imaging could be an assistant imaging to the ISAR imaging.

articleTitle: The Study of High Power Microwave Pulse Propagation in the Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the propagation of the high power microwave pulse is numerical simulated in each layer of ionosphere. FDTD method for solving this problem will waste great time and memory. Therefore, we used PSTD algorithm to solve the equations of cold plasma. The results are accord with the previous. The validity of PSTD algorithm is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Compact Modified-Meander Resonator for Microwave Bandpass Filter with Harmonic-Suppression
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This research presents a compact modified-meander resonator, has applied to microwave narrow bandpass filter in 3G mobile based-station which operates at 1.95 GHz and 60 MHz of bandwidth. The features of 26-percent smaller-sized and harmonic-suppression have proposed. The reasonable of harmonic-suppression has demonstrated.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Compound Waveguide Slot Coupler Using the MPSTD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the MPSTD algorithm is applied to model the compound slot located in the common broad wall of X band rectangular waveguides. The resonant length of the compound slot and the S parameters of the coupler are analyzed by MPSTD. The numerical results indicate that the MPSTD algorithm is accurate and efficient to analyze the compound waveguide slot coupler.

articleTitle: Study of Ground Defect PBG Structure in Cylindrical Microstrip Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the application of PBG structure to cylindrical rectangular microstrip patch antennas is studied. Characteristics of square holes and circle holes etched in cylindrical ground are invested for different size. The results indicate the effectiveness of the PBG structure for suppressing harmonic and surface wave.

articleTitle: Analysis of EM scattering characteristics from 2D electrically large objects using characteristic basis function method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: Characteristic basis function method (CBFM) is a novel approach for the efficient solution of electromagnetic scattering problems. In this paper, CBFM combined with the domain decomposition technique is used to calculate the radar cross sections from 2D electrically large conducting cylinder and dielectric cylinder. It is shown that the numerical results presented in this paper are in good agreement with that achieved by the traditional method of moments, while the computational efficiency is improved greatly.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Design of Double Folded-Slot Antenna with Back Ground Conductor
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A novel ultra-wideband coplanar waveguide-fed double folded-slot antenna with back ground conductor is proposed and studied. With the finite element method, the dependences of the return loss on length of radiation arm and slot spacing are investigated. The calculated results show that the impedance bandwidth, determined by -10 dB return loss, of the proposed double folded-slot antenna can be more than 30%, and can be used for the engineering.

articleTitle: Research and Simulation on Effect of Turbulence to Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, research on effect of turbulence to optical communication through the analysis of atmospheric turbulence, and display the optical plot in time. This is very important to optimize capability of optical communication.

articleTitle: The Design of High Gain Dipole Antenna with Metamaterial Cover
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we analyze a metamaterial cover based on metal wire array, and use it to increase the gain of dipole from 2.15 dB to 14.5 dB, with narrow beam and low side-lobe levels. And then provide the use of metal strips etched by printed circuit board (PCB) process to substitute the metal wires in order to reduce the weight and be easy in processing. The structure of metal strip array can also greatly increase the gain of dipole and possess good practical engineering application.

articleTitle: Laser Radar Cross-Section of Conducting Targets Using Horizontal Polarization
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This work presents a study to handle the behavior of radar cross section (RCS) of partially convex targets of large sizes up to five wavelengths in free space. The nature of incident wave is an important factor in the remote sensing and radar detection applications. To investigate the effects of incident wave nature on the RCS, scattering problems of plane and beam wave incidences are considered. Targets are taking large sizes to be bigger enough than the beam width with putting into consideration a horizontal incident wave polarization (E-wave incidence). The effects of the target configuration together with the beam width on the laser RCS compared to the case with the plane wave incidence are numerically analyzed. Therefore, we will be able to have some sort of control on radar detection using beam wave incidence. .

articleTitle: Preliminary Research on Large Switch Number Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The differences of analysis methods between two kinds of reconfigurable antenna, the small switch number reconfigurable antenna (SSN-RA) and the large switch number reconfigurable antenna (LSN-RA), are discussed first. From the present general research methods on LSNRA, adopting the statistical method to determinate distribution characteristic of LSN-RA radiation pattern is illuminated then. The method can extend to quantify other performance parameters of antenna, at last the design of experiments methodology is introduced to estimates the effects of switch failure of LSN-RA.

articleTitle: A RF Small Pulse Signal Processing Circuit Based-on SCM
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a RF pulse signal processing circuit based on SCM(single chip microcomputer). The pulse is high-frequency-modulated, low-amplitude and narrow-time-width. The circuit could process the pulse when its width r > 0.4 mus , duty-cycle D< 1/2000, and amplitude P ges 2mv (after demodulated). By designing the time on which the SCM answers an interruption, the circuit could eliminate disturbance between two pulses efficiently,. Experiments have proved that the system is effective, credible and economical.

articleTitle: A Phase-only Direct Data Domain Algorithm Based on the Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient Method
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A phase-only direct data domain least square (D3LS) algorithm based on the nonlinear conjugate gradient (CG) method is presented. The cost function is obtained via the normal D3LS algorithm as a first step, and then optimized with the nonlinear CG method to determine the optimum weight vector finally. As a phase-only adaptive algorithm, the proposed algorithm has a better simplicity on hardware implementation than conventional algorithms. Moreover, it processes only a single data snapshot with no use for the formation of the sample covariance matrix and matrix inversion operation. Therefore, it may be so effective in real-time processing. Simulation results show the proposed algorithm has a good signal recovery and interferences nulling performance.

articleTitle: Spectrum BRDF and its Application in Visible Light Scattering of Spatial Object
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: The spectral bi-directional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of some satellite coating material and solar plane samples in the band from 380 to 780 nanometres is measured with relative measurement in the laboratory. The spectrum BRDF which can characterize the spectrum reflectance property of samples is obtained by weighting the measured spectral BRDF by the spectral irradiance of the incident spectrum. A new method to calculate the visible light scattering of spatial object is introduced with the aid of the spectrum BRDF. As an application example, the visible light scattering of a simple satellite model is calculated.

articleTitle: Aspects of Statistical Radar Polarimetry
publicationTitle: 2006 7th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation & EM Theory
abstract: A comparison between the Kennaugh matrix and the covariance matrix formulation of second-order moment radar polarimetry reveals fundamental relationships between power and variance aspects of bistatic and monostatic radar scattering from randomly distributed targets.
